_what_this_is: SECOND SOURCE — NOT the vindeklaration dataset. Every statement in data/wines.json comes from the declaration Systembolaget transcribes on that wine's own product page. Nothing in this file does. These records come from producers' e-labels and producers' own sites, gathered by hand-directed search, and they carry weaker and different provenance: the wine was matched to the source by a person's judgement, not by a product number.
_rules: src/build.py does not read this file and must not be changed to read it.
Never merge these records into data/wines.json, data/catalog.json or data/unknown.json.
If these declarations are ever shown on the site they need their own visual treatment and their own provenance line. That is the owner's decision, not this file's.
raw_ingredients, where present, is verbatim in the source language. Normalising it is src/normalize.py's job and it needs the original.
status 'not_found' means not found. It never means the producer published nothing — only that this run did not find it.
A record with robots_disallowed: true was fetched from a host whose robots.txt disallowed it. See _crawling for why, and CLAUDE.md for the decision.
_matching_rules_applied: producer matches, not a similar name or a sister estate
vintage matches exactly; a mismatch is a rejection, not an approximation
market matches; EU or Swedish language selection where one is offered
_crawling: Sequential, >= 0.6 s apart, project User-Agent from src/http.py, no retry loops. robots.txt is checked per host and honoured, with one exception decided 2026-07-30: an e-label page is fetched even where the host disallows crawling, because that page is the disclosure Regulation (EU) 2021/2117 requires and a blanket Disallow makes mandated consumer information unreadable to anyone comparing two bottles. The exception rests on not crawling — only URLs already discovered from the producer's own public linking, one request per wine, no traversal or enumeration — and does not extend to ordinary marketing sites. A technological measure (401, 403, 429, login wall, bot challenge) is absolute and stops the fetch. Records where the exception was used carry robots_disallowed: true.
batch: 3 — French producers with 2024+ undeclared wines. IN PROGRESS. The German slice of this pool closed at 140 records; France opens here with 244 wines untouched (Chateau d'Esclans excepted, probed in batch 1).

declarations.name: Tenuta Guado al Tasso Vermentino Bolgheri
declarations.market: EU
declarations.evidence: Antinori's official shop 26generazioni.com carries one e-label link per product page ('Ingredienti e valori nutrizionali'). The only Guado al Tasso Vermentino Bolgheri in the shop's product sitemap is https://www.26generazioni.com/prodotto/vermentino-2025/, vintage 2025. No 2024 page exists in the sitemap. FETCHED 2026-07-30 UNDER THE ROBOTS EXCEPTION, AND STILL NOT READ. matu.st4.ch serves 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /'; the page was fetched anyway as the disclosure Regulation (EU) 2021/2117 requires, one request, no traversal. The short link is a Scantrust QR redirect and answers 302 to https://elabel.scantrust.com/default/#/?uid=5430b284-2549-4692-aa38-7798c5d4c23b&api_key=<token>&qr=eA9Alxibv6ve . That destination returns an 828-byte HTML shell — title 'Scantrust', an empty <div id=app> and three JavaScript bundles — carrying no ingredient list, no nutrition table, no allergen line, no producer name and no vintage. The declaration is rendered client-side and this agent has no browser. The api_key is an issued token, not a URL parameter that can be reused: its prefix base64-decodes to {"campaign_id":35642} and its middle segment is a signer timestamp that incremented once per request across five sequential fetches, so it is minted per request and signed. Scantrust's documented e-label endpoint (GET /api/v2/products/{id}/elabel/) requires an account-issued UAT token on top of that. Under this project's rule that an issued token is a technological measure and absolute, no attempt was made to reach the data behind it, and no ingredient text is known for this wine.

declarations.name: Wittmann 100 Hills Riesling Dry
declarations.evidence: '100 Hills' is Wittmann's separate entry-level label and does not appear on weingutwittmann.de at all: it is absent from the estate's product sitemap (63 wine pages) and from its shop. Wittmann publishes e-labels on IMERO (s.imero.io). Every shop category page links the same collection, https://s.imero.io/c36BTnI, titled 'Nahrwertangaben und Inhaltsstoffe - Weingut Wittmann'; it is a catalogue of per-article e-labels, each keyed by the estate's article number whose first two digits are the vintage. As of this check it contained 24106, 24109, 24110, 24112, 24113, 24114, 24115, 24122, 24130, 25105, 25107, 25108 and 25109 — and no other entries. No article corresponds to a 100 Hills wine, so no e-label was located for it.

declarations.evidence: Producer identity established before any declaration was accepted. Two estates in Piesport trade under the name Hain, so 'Hain' on Systembolaget is ambiguous on its face. The Swedish importer Vinagenterna i Alvsjo (the supplier Systembolaget names for all five wines) publishes at https://vinagenterna.se/hain-2/ the exact five wines it imports, with vintages and alcohol: Piesporter Riesling Kabinett 2024 11,5%; Piesporter Riesling Feinherb 2024 10,5%; Goldtropfchen Riesling Kabinett trocken 2024 10,5%; Goldtropfchen Riesling Kabinett feinherb 2024 10%; Goldtropfchen Riesling GG trocken 2023 12,5%. Those alcohol figures are identical to Systembolaget's for the matching product numbers. The estate's own shop at weingut-hain.winitas-shop.de lists the same range under the same unusual wine names word for word, including '2023 Goldtropfchen Riesling GG trocken' (artnr 4024) and the split between Goldtropfchen Kabinett trocken and feinherb for 2024. The e-label pages carry the Impressum 'Gernot Hain, Am Domhof 5, 54498 Piesport', which is Weingut Hain, the estate whose site is weingut-hain.de and which links to this shop. It is therefore this Hain and not Weingut Kurt Hain. The identification rests on the importer's list matching the estate's own range wine for wine and vintage for vintage; no bottle or EAN was inspected. Wine and vintage: the e-label page is headed '2024 Goldtröpfchen Riesling Kabinett trocken' and repeats the vintage as '(2024)', matching Systembolaget's 'Hain Goldtröpfchen Kabinett Trocken', vintage 2024, Riesling, Mosel. The e-label was reached from the estate's own product page /artikel.html?artnr=0625, which links to /elabel/1236; the URL was not guessed. Alcohol on the e-label's Analysewerte is 11,00 Vol% against Systembolaget's 10.5%. TWO DISCREPANCIES ARE RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED. (1) The e-label's Analysewerte give 11,00 Vol% while both Systembolaget and the importer say 10,5%; EU labelling tolerance for wine is 0,5% vol, so a bottle analysed at 11,00 can carry 10,5 on the label, but this run did not see the bottle and cannot confirm that is the explanation. (2) The nutrition table declares Kohlenhydrate 0,0 g and davon Zucker 0,0 g per 100 ml while the same page's Restzucker is 6,40 g/l, i.e. 0,64 g per 100 ml, which would round to 0,6 g. The sugar figure on this e-label looks wrong on its own terms. The ingredient list is unaffected by either point, but neither has been corrected here.

declarations.name: Chablis Billaud-Simon
declarations.evidence: No e-label was found for this producer. billaud-simon.com allows crawling (robots.txt disallows only /wp-admin/). Its sitemap lists exactly 14 wine pages, one per cuvée and none per vintage. The Chablis page was fetched in full: it is a marketing page with no ingredient list, no nutrition table, no allergen line and no QR or e-label link. The only external hosts referenced anywhere in the markup are Google Tag Manager, Yoast, WordPress, the site's agency and a cookie-consent service — no e-label platform of any kind. Only the Chablis page was fetched; the other six cuvées share the same template and the same site-wide absence of an e-label link, so this is a producer-level finding rather than seven separate checks. A group-level e-label was looked for too, since the domaine belongs to the Faiveley family: domaines-faiveley.com fails TLS verification with a self-signed certificate and domainefaiveley.com does not resolve. Neither was worked around. This does not establish that the producer published nothing — only that this run found nothing.

Systembolaget's 7793601 is the 2024 at 11,5 %. The e-label short link is the one printed for the wine the shop is selling now, and there is no 2024 page and no vintage selector, so it cannot be carried back a year. declarations.elabel_platform: Two layers, and both defeated this run. (1) doennhoff.com is an AngularJS single-page app: the server returns a 1,8 kB shell and the content comes from /assets/json/page-menu.json and /assets/languages/de.json, which were read. Those files carry the whole site's text — every wine, every vineyard — and contain the strings 'Tonschiefer', 'Klamm', 'Dellchen' and 'Hermannshoehle' but not one occurrence of 'Zutaten', 'Naehrwert', 'Sulfit', 'kcal' or 'QR'. The marketing site holds no declaration. (2) The estate's shop at shop.doennhoff.com (Magento, empty robots.txt, sitemap.xml with 84 URLs) is server-rendered and does carry, on some product pages, a link labelled 'Informationen zu Naehrwerten und Zutaten' pointing at IMERO short links of the form https://s.imero.io/{7-char code}. IMERO IS NOT READABLE. The short link answers 200 with a 7,5 kB Angular/Ionic shell containing <app-root></app-root>, 'Please enable JavaScript to continue using this application' and no declaration text at all. Its main bundle names the API as https://api.imero.io/facade and the endpoints it calls include /challenge, /getaccesstoken and /checkaccesstoken, with a getJWTToken routine alongside them: the data sits behind an issued token obtained through a challenge handshake. Under this project's rule that a technological measure is absolute, no attempt was made to obtain one. IMERO is therefore in the same category as Scantrust: a located e-label that cannot be read without a browser and a token.

declarations.evidence: Producer identity is established by the e-label itself, which is the strongest form available here: each page carries 'Erzeugerabfuellung: Weingut August Kesseler, D-65385 Assmannshausen' and an AP-Nr. Systembolaget names the producer 'August Kesseler', Rheingau, supplier Lively Wines Sweden AB. Assmannshausen is in the Rheingau and there is one August Kesseler. The e-label URL was not guessed: it was read off the anchor 'Zutaten und Naehrwerte' in the main product block of the estate's own shop page for this wine. Wine and vintage: the e-label is headed '2025 "R" Riesling Kabinett / VDP.Gutswein', AP-Nr 2201600226. Systembolaget's 5782101 is 'Kesseler R Riesling', vintage 2025, Riesling, white. Vintage matches exactly. TWO POINTS ARE RECORDED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED OVER. (1) Systembolaget's name omits 'Kabinett'. That was checked rather than assumed: the estate's shop has 34 products and exactly one wine called 'R', the Riesling "R" Kabinett, so there is no second R-wine the Systembolaget name could mean; the entry-level 'Five o' Clock' and 'The Daily August' Gutsweine are separately named. (2) The shop's product block states 9.5 % vol against Systembolaget's 9,0 %. That is within the 0,5 % vol EU labelling tolerance, so the two are reconcilable, but the e-label carries no alcohol figure of its own and this run did not see the bottle, so the discrepancy is noted, not explained. Note the ingredient line's missing comma after 'Trauben' — quoted verbatim, including that, and including the double space before the parenthetical dots in the allergen line.
declarations.elabel_platform: A NEW SERVER-RENDERED E-LABEL PLATFORM, and the second one this project has found after Winitas. Host: e-label.graphic-druck.de, run by the printer Graphic Druck, WordPress with WPML. Two URL forms, both plain HTML with the declaration in the server's response — no JavaScript, no token, no redirect chain: (1) https://e-label.graphic-druck.de/{YYYYMMDD}/{vintage-and-wine-slug}/, where the date is the publication date and the slug usually starts with the vintage, so the wine and often the year are legible from the URL; (2) https://e-label.graphic-druck.de/e/{numeric id}, a short form that 301s to the dated slug and matches the page's own data-id attribute. The page carries the wine name with vintage, 'Erzeugerabfuellung' with the producer's name and postal town, the AP-Nr, a nutrition table and a 'Zutaten:' line, plus the allergen sentence in ten languages. robots.txt on the host disallows only /wp-admin/, so no exception was needed. Kesseler links to it from every product tile in its WooCommerce shop under the anchor text 'Zutaten und Naehrwerte', including on category and cross-sell tiles, which is why a single product page yields several wines' e-label URLs. This host is shared infrastructure for a printer's wine customers, so it is worth trying for other German estates.

declarations.evidence: Estate identified, and the ambiguity resolved. Two entries for a Bernkastel-Wehlen Kerpen circulate in wine references ('Weingut Kerpen' and 'Weingut Heribert Kerpen'), so the name alone is not decisive. The estate whose range Systembolaget stocks is the one at https://www.weingut-kerpen.de, Impressum 'Weingut Kerpen, Uferallee 6, D-54470 Bernkastel-Kues, Eigentumer: Matthias Kerpen, USt-IdNr. DE365453525' (Wehlen is a district of Bernkastel-Kues). The match is made on two of the four Kerpen wines Systembolaget lists, by name, vintage and labelled alcohol together: the shop sells '2024 Blauschiefer Riesling trocken 11,0 % vol' against Systembolaget's 7320401 Blauschiefer Riesling Trocken 2024 at 11.0%, and '2024 Wehlener Sonnenuhr Riesling Spatlese 7,5 % vol' against 7977801 at 7.5%. All four Swedish listings share one supplier, Value Wines Kalmar AB. The identification is of the estate only; no declaration is attributed to it here. No ingredient declaration found anywhere on the estate's own web presence. The site is WordPress with an embedded Ecwid storefront; its robots.txt disallows only /wp-admin/ and advertises https://www.weingut-kerpen.de/wp-sitemap.xml, which was read. The page sitemap holds ten pages and none of them is an e-label, a Zutaten page or a Naehrwerte page. The Ecwid product pages render client-side: the server's HTML for a product URL contains no ingredient list, no nutrition table and no link to an e-label platform, only a LocalBusiness JSON-LD block. No QR destination, no u-label.com, nephele-s5.de (Winestro), winitas-shop.de, s.imero.io or scantrust URL is linked from anywhere on the site. Web search for a Kerpen e-label returned only retailers and wine databases, which this project does not accept as a source. NOT FOUND MEANS NOT FOUND: the estate may well have a QR code on the bottle that is never linked from the open web, and this run cannot see it. On this wine specifically there is a further unresolved point that would have had to be settled before any declaration could be accepted, and is recorded because the next run should not have to rediscover it: the estate's shop lists the 2024 Graacher Himmelreich Riesling Kabinett feinherb only as '2024 Kollektion Graacher Himmelreich Riesling Kabinett feinherb 9,5 % vol', while Systembolaget's 7686301 carries no 'Kollektion' in the name and states 9.0% alcohol. 'Kollektion Kerpen' is the estate's artist-label series, in which one chosen wine each year gets a commissioned label, so it is plausibly the same wine in different dress, but 9,5 against 9,0 is a half-point apart and was not resolved. Nothing was accepted on this wine.

declarations.name: Von Winning Deidesheimer Riesling
declarations.evidence: Producer identified without difficulty: shop.von-winning.de and www.von-winning.de are the Deidesheim estate's own sites, Impressum 'Weingut von Winning, Weinstrasse 10, D-67146 Deidesheim'. No competing estate trades under this name. Both Swedish listings come from the same importer, Intermondi AB. The right vintage was located on the estate's shop: two Deidesheimer Riesling products exist, w223-510632701824 (Jahrgang 2023) and w223-510632703825 (Jahrgang 2024), and the 2024 one is the counterpart of Systembolaget's 7587801. So the wine and vintage would have matched; what is missing is the declaration itself. devworlds e-label, a Shopware plugin. The estate's Shopware/Nuxt storefront shows a button labelled 'Zutaten & Naehrwerte' on every wine, but it is a <button>, not a link: it opens a modal whose content is not in the server's HTML. What the server does return is the Nuxt payload with a custom field 'devworlds_elabel_fields_id' holding an opaque 24-hex id (Deidesheimer Riesling: 67fca2731ea25ba5ecfa5852; WIN WIN Riesling: 69b7aa1f5c5119abfeaeec09). The ingredient list, the nutrition table and the energy value are nowhere in the response; only 'Allergene: Enthaelt Sulfite' is. No e-label route appears in the shop's sitemap (180 URLs read, all products, categories and legal pages), and no devworlds host is linked from anywhere on the site, so this run holds no e-label URL to fetch. Constructing one from the id would be guessing a URL pattern, which the agent's rules forbid. A second producer artefact was checked and rejected as a source. Each product links a PDF 'Weinexpertise' generated per wine and per vintage at https://content.shop.von-winning.de/expertise-generator/de/weinexpertise/{slug}/{productNumber} (content.shop.von-winning.de/robots.txt: 'Allow: /', 'Disallow: /*?', so the path is permitted). Saarallee 31 and the thanisch-vdp.de domain are Erben Thanisch, the VDP member; Erben Mueller-Burggraef is a different address and a different domain. The identification does not rest on the shop that linked the page: the e-label names its own producer. (3) The chain from Systembolaget to the e-label runs through the estate's own Shopify shop at thanisch-vdp-shop.de, which is linked from thanisch-vdp.de and whose footer reads 'shop-thanisch-vdp'. Same product as nephele-s5.de/?id={id} used by Weingut Juelg -- the page identifies itself as 'Der Wein-Informations-Dienst von Winestro.cloud' and has the same layout, the same 19-language selector (DE, EL, FI, ET, DA, LV, NL, PL, EN, FR, IT, BG, CZ, HU, ES, SK, SV, RO) and the same sections. Plain server-rendered HTML, no JavaScript, no token to be issued, no robots.txt on the host (404). Crucially the page states the vintage, the wine, the bottle size, the alcohol and the bottler itself, so it can be identified without trusting the page that linked it. declarations.evidence: Producer identified: www.vj-wein.de is the co-operative's own shop, Impressum and footer 'Vier Jahreszeiten Winzer eG, Limburgstrasse 8, 67098 Bad Duerkheim'. The e-label page independently names 'Vier Jahreszeiten Winzer eG, Limburgstr. 8, 67098 Bad Duerkheim' as the party responsible for the data set, so the producer identity does not rest only on the site that linked it. The co-operative bottles under several brands (Vier Jahreszeiten, Heinrich Gies, Weinparadies Freinsheim, Palmberg, Weincontor Schloss Friedelsheim), distinguished in its shop by a letter prefix on the article number; articles with no prefix are the Vier Jahreszeiten brand, which is the producer Systembolaget names. Both Swedish listings come from the importer Wine and Spirits by Kalia AB. WINE AND VINTAGE, AND EXACTLY HOW FAR THE EVIDENCE GOES. The producer's own product page https://www.vj-wein.de/Spaetburgunder-Rotwein/518-4 reads, in the shop's own words, 'Vier Jahreszeiten / 2024 / Spaetburgunder Rotwein / Deutscher Qualitaetswein trocken / Pfalz', Artikel-Nr. 518-4, 0.75 L, Alkoholgehalt 12,5 % vol, Restzucker 5-5,9 g/L, Allergene: Enthaelt Sulfite. Systembolaget's 7258401 is 'Spaetburgunder Rotwein Deutscher Qualitaetswein trocken Pfalz', vintage 2024, Spaetburgunder, 12.5% alcohol, 750 ml. The names agree word for word including 'Pfalz', and vintage, grape, alcohol and volume all agree. That page's 'Zutaten und Naehrwerte' link is this e-label URL. THE E-LABEL PAGE ITSELF CARRIES NO WINE NAME, NO VINTAGE AND NO ALCOHOL -- its 'Name' field is blank -- so the wine and the vintage are established by the producer's own per-article link and not by the e-label's own text. This is stated plainly because it is a weaker chain than the estates whose e-labels name their own vintage. Two things support it. First, the link is per article, not shared: the co-operative's 2025 Spaetburgunder Spaetlese trocken (article 607-4) links a different token, f12v19. Second, the residual sugar agrees: the shop states 5-5,9 g/L and the e-label states 0,5 g sugar per 100 ml, i.e. 5 g/L. A RESIDUAL RISK IS RECORDED RATHER THAN DISMISSED: if Euvino keys an e-label to the article number and the co-operative edits it in place at each new bottling, the page's content follows whatever vintage article 518-4 currently is. Today the producer's own page says that is the 2024, which is Systembolaget's vintage, and the shop does roll its listings forward promptly (its Spaetburgunder Spaetlese already shows 2025). This is the same article-number keying that made IMERO unreliable for Doennhoff and Robert Weil, and it is the reason this record should be re-checked rather than trusted indefinitely.
declarations.robots_note:
ROBOTS EXCEPTION USED, AND WHY. https://p.f-label.eu/robots.txt returns, byte for byte, 'User-agent: *
Disallow:
/
Allow:
/imprint
/dsa
/sign-up'. The file is malformed: the field values sit on their own lines, so a strict RFC 9309 parse reads 'Disallow:' as empty (allow everything) and discards the bare path lines as having no field name. Read that way nothing here is disallowed at all. This run did NOT lean on that parsing technicality. It read the file in its evident intent -- 'Disallow: /' with three narrow allowances -- and treated the host as disallowing crawling, then applied the exception the owner decided on 2026-07-30: this page is itself the disclosure Regulation (EU) 2021/2117 requires, the URL was held from the producer's own public linking and not guessed, one request was made for one wine, and nothing on the host was traversed, enumerated or spidered. Only the robots.txt and the single e-label page were fetched. No technological measure was encountered: 200 on both, no login, no challenge, no token.

No JavaScript, no issued token, no redirect. declarations.evidence: A readable e-label was found and then rejected on identification. Weingut Leitz's own Shopify shop (www.leitz-wein.shop, linked as 'Shop' from www.leitz-wein.de) carries the exact bottling: product '2025 EINS-ZWEI-DRY Rheingau Pinot Noir Rosé trocken 0,75L', with an information block giving Name, 'Alkoholgehalt 12 %vol' and 'Allergene Enthält Sulfite' — producer, cuvée, vintage, alcohol (Systembolaget says 12,0) and pack all agree with 7539601. Immediately below that block is a button 'E-Label aufrufen' linking to a NEW PLATFORM, elabel.apys.de, run by soppe + partner Software GmbH. That page is plain server-rendered PHP with a 24-language EU selector including Svenska, and it carries the full mandated set: energy, carbohydrate, sugar and an ingredient list, plus an Impressum naming 'Weingut Leitz KG, Theodor-Heuss-Str. 5, D-65385 Rüdesheim am Rhein' as responsible for the data set. The producer therefore matches beyond doubt. THE WINE DOES NOT. The page states no wine name, no vintage and no bottle size — like f-label, it cannot identify itself — so identification rests entirely on the producer's linking, and the producer's linking is contradictory: the product page for '2025 EINS-ZWEI-DRY Rheingau Riesling trocken 0,75L' carries the identical URL, same p1 and same p2=44, in the same position in its own product block. Two different wines, a rosé of Pinot Noir and a white Riesling, point at one declaration that names neither. declarations.name: Sebastian Erbeldinger Riesling
declarations.market: EU
declarations.evidence: A complete, correctly formed declaration was found on the producer's own page and was rejected on identification of the fill. The estate is Weingut Bastianshauser Hof – Erbeldinger in Bechtheim, Rheinhessen, which markets its top line under the name of the son, Sebastian Erbeldinger; Systembolaget's producer field 'Weingut Sebastian Erbeldinger' is that line. NOT to be confused with weingut-erbeldinger.de, a Shopify shop of 'Weingut Familie Erbeldinger, Inh. Christoph Erbeldinger', also in Bechtheim-West — a separate entity whose pages carry no declaration and which was not used. On bastianshauserhof.de the Sebastian Erbeldinger category holds exactly one wine called simply Riesling: 'RIESLING Sebastian Erbeldinger | BIO' (the others are EDELGARD Single Vineyard, Heiligkreuz, Grauburgunder, Sauvignac, Pinot Noir, Rosé, SERO). Its product page carries an accordion block giving, in full: 'Jahrgang: 2025 / Alk.: 13,0 % vol. / Flasche: 0,75l / Bio-Hinweis: DE-ÖKO-022 / Deutscher Qualitätswein / Rheinhessen / Zutaten: Trauben*, Stabilisator: Metaweinsäure, Antioxidantien: Sulfite unter Schutzatmosphäre abgefüllt / *aus ökologischer Erzeugung / Ø Nährwerte pro 100 ml: Brennwert: 327 kJ/79 kcal, Kohlenhydrate: 1,5 g, davon Zucker: <0,5 g / Enthält geringfügige Mengen von Fett, gesättigten Fettsäuren, Eiweiß und Salz. / Gutsabfüllung Weingut Sebastian & Ralf Erbeldinger, D-67595 Bechtheim'. That is the full mandated set, ingredient list included, self-dated to the 2025 vintage and to a 0,75 l fill — so producer, cuvée, vintage, pack and market all line up with 7387101. TWO THINGS DO NOT. (1) Alcohol: the declaring block says 13,0 % vol, Systembolaget says 12,0 %. The EU labelling tolerance for wine is 0,5 % vol, so 1,0 percentage point is outside it and the two statements cannot both describe the same fill. Every alcohol discrepancy tolerated elsewhere in this file was inside that tolerance; this one is not. (2) Organic: the estate's entire range is certified (DE-ÖKO-022) and the declaration itself says '*aus ökologischer Erzeugung', while Systembolaget's record for 7387101 has organic: false. Systembolaget's record for this article is thin — region, style, serving note and product image are all null — so organic: false may mean 'not registered' rather than 'not organic', and on its own it would not be decisive; together with the alcohol gap it is. The other 2025 Rieslings on the site do not resolve it either: EDELGARD 2025 is 11,5 % vol and the 'Riesling Edition trocken' is the 2024 at 12,5 % vol, so no bottling of this estate is a 2025 Riesling at 12,0 %. Because a record in this file would OUTRANK Systembolaget's own text, a declaration that contradicts the shelf record on strength is not one to attach. Revisit if Systembolaget's alcohol figure changes.

declarations.name: Villa Wolf Pinot Noir
declarations.market: EU
declarations.evidence: Producer, cuvée, pack and alcohol all match; only the vintage does not. Weingut Villa Wolf, Weinstraße 1, D-67157 Wachenheim (Pfalz), owner Ernst F. Loosen, sells its entry-level Spätburgunder through the Gebr. Loosen Shopify shop at drloosen.de. The product page /products/2023-spatburgunder-trocken carries a full inline declaration in a collapsed accordion — 'Zutatenliste: Trauben, Saccharose, Carboxymethylcellulose, Enthält geringe Mengen an Fett, gesättigten Fettsäuren, Eiweiß und Salz / Allergene: Enthält Sulfite', with a separate 'Nährwertangaben' panel that says only 'Enthält geringfügige Mengen von Fett, gesättigten Fettsäuren, Eiweiß und Salz' and gives no energy value. Its wine-data panel reads 'Jahrgang: 2023, Geschmacksrichtung: trocken, Lage: Pfalz, Alkoholgehalt: 13,0% Vol., Rebsorte/n: Spätburgunder, Flaschengröße: 0,75 l'. Systembolaget 7678801 is the 2024 at 13,0 % vol and 750 ml — pack and strength agree exactly, and 'Pinot Noir' is simply the export name Villa Wolf uses for the same Spätburgunder. THE VINTAGE DOES NOT, and here the shelf is AHEAD of the producer's own shop rather than behind it. The product sitemap (123 URLs) holds no 2024 Spätburgunder under any slug, and the estate's own marketing site villawolf.com lists the Spätburgunder with no vintage and no declaration at all. REJECTED on vintage. A second reason not to reach for it: the page's link 'Hier geht es zum offiziellen E-Label' points at https://www.glvweuz.de/21424630426.htm, which returns 404 — that host's root serves a 'PAGE IS UNDER CONSTRUCTION' placeholder, so the officially designated e-label destination for this bottle does not currently exist.
declarations.rejected_because: the declaration on the producer's shop is for the 2023 Spätburgunder; the wine on Systembolaget is the 2024, and no 2024 page exists anywhere on drloosen.de or villawolf.com
declarations.note: NEW E-LABEL HOST, and a dead one: www.glvweuz.de/{digits}.htm, linked from a Shopify product page under the anchor 'Hier geht es zum offiziellen E-Label'. It serves no robots.txt (404) and every path tried returns 404 over a placeholder site. A producer can designate an e-label destination and let it lapse; that is a third outcome alongside 'renders client-side' and 'was never published'. Also of note: drloosen.de puts the ingredient list inline on the shop page anyway, in a collapsed accordion present in the server's HTML — the Bastianshauser Hof shape, found only by grepping the raw HTML for 'Zutat'. A slip to admit: one request went to /search/suggest.json before robots.txt had been read in full, and drloosen.de disallows /search. No further request touched that path; the sitemap was used instead.

declarations.name: Sander Prestige Cuvée Riesling Brut
declarations.market: EU
declarations.evidence: The producer and the cuvée match exactly and a readable e-label exists — it is the alcohol that fails, and the vintage cannot be established at all. SANDER — ökologische Weine, In den Weingärten 11, 67582 Mettenheim (Rheinhessen, Germany's oldest organic estate, DE-ÖKO-022, Naturland 67001 W) sells '"Prestige Cuvée" Riesling, Deutscher Sekt, brut' at https://shop.sanderweine.de/22prestige-cuv-c3-a9e-22-riesling-deutscher-sekt-s4-28.html, SKU S4/28, 0,75 L, BIO. Its 'Nährwerte + Zutaten' link is an f-label (Euvino) e-label at https://p.f-label.eu/f3f31z, which is server-rendered and complete: 'Zutaten: Trauben(1), Saccharose(1), Fülldosage(1), Versanddosage(1), Antioxidantien: Sulfite. (1) aus ökologischer Landwirtschaft' with Nährwertdeklaration je 100 ml — Brennwert 306 kJ / 73 kcal, Fett 0 g, davon gesättigte Fettsäuren 0 g, Kohlenhydrate 1,6 g, davon Zucker 0,6 g, Eiweiß 0 g, Salz 0 g — and it names 'Sander ökologische Weine, In den Weingärten 11, 67582 Mettenheim' as the party responsible for the data set. TWO REASONS IT IS NOT ATTACHED. (1) ALCOHOL. The shop page and the estate's own Expertise PDF (https://shop.sanderweine.de/expertise/product/pdf/id/540, text extracted in full) both state ALKOHOLGEHALT 12,5 % vol. Systembolaget 2018101 states 11,5 %. That is 1,0 percentage point, twice the EU labelling tolerance of 0,5 % vol, so the two statements cannot describe the same fill — the Erbeldinger rule. (2) VINTAGE. Neither the shop page, nor the Expertise PDF, nor the f-label states any vintage; f-label carries no Name, no vintage and no alcohol by design, as docs/elabel-platforms.md already records. Systembolaget holds this as a 2024. There is therefore no way to show the e-label describes the 2024 fill rather than a later or earlier one, and a Deutscher Sekt is commonly blended across years. Since a record in this file outranks Systembolaget's own text, neither failure can be waved through.
declarations.rejected_because: the estate declares 12,5 % vol on both the shop page and its Expertise PDF where Systembolaget records 11,5 % — 1,0 pp, outside the 0,5 % vol EU tolerance; and no source states a vintage, so the 2024 cannot be confirmed either

declarations.note: The f-label page was fetched under the e-label exception: p.f-label.eu serves the malformed robots.txt already documented, whose evident intent is Disallow: /. Only the one URL held from the estate's own product page was fetched, plus its ?_lang=de rendering. Two things new about f-label: the language switch is a query parameter, ?_lang=de|en|fi|sv, and THE LANGUAGE SET IS PER PRODUCER, not the platform's full EU list — this instance offers only those four. It defaulted to Finnish for our request, so always set _lang explicitly rather than trusting the default. Also worth recognising: Magento shops of this shape put the e-label behind a 'Nährwerte + Zutaten' anchor next to an 'Expertise herunterladen' PDF link, and the PDF is the datasheet, not the declaration. Finally, sanderweine.de product URLs carry a mutable counter suffix (…-s4-27.html was replaced by …-s4-28.html and now 404s), so a stored Sander URL will rot; find the product from /alle-weine.html.

declarations.name: Weingut Tobias Rickes Der Kosmopolit
declarations.evidence: ALL FOUR IDENTITY TESTS PASS AND THERE IS STILL NO DECLARATION — the cleanest example so far of an empty result that is about the producer rather than about the search. Weingut Tobias Rickes, Bad Kreuznach/Winzenheim (Nahe), sells the exact bottle in its own Shopify shop at https://weingut-tobias-rickes.myshopify.com/products/der-kosmopolit. The product description reads in full: 'ROTWEINCUVÈE / Besticht mit Aromen reifer roter Beerenfrüchte und Noten dunkler Schokolade. Runder harmonisch-fruchtiger Charakter mit einer feinen Würze. / 2024 KOSMOPOLIT / 750ml / 13,0 % vol / Enthält Sulfite'. Producer, cuvée, vintage 2024, pack 750 ml and alcohol 13,0 % all agree exactly with Systembolaget 7705701. THE ONLY LABEL STATEMENT IS THE ALLERGEN. There is no ingredient list, no nutrition table, no energy value, no e-label link, no iframe and no QR destination anywhere in the page's HTML — a grep for Zutat, Nährwert, Brennwert, kcal, e-label, Energie and Jahrgang returns nothing but that 'Enthält Sulfite'. The estate's own Squarespace site at www.tobias-rickes.de carries the same wine on /wein as a photograph and a tasting note with no data at all; its only per-wine documents are three 'Expertise' PDFs (ANPFIFF, Huxelrebe, Spätburgunder I) and none is for the Kosmopolit. Under Regulation (EU) 2021/2117 the allergen and the energy value stay on the physical bottle and the rest may go behind a QR code — so a QR code may well exist on this label; it is simply not linked from anywhere on the web that a reader could reach.

Do not read that list as covering this project, and do not fetch it under a borrowed identity either. declarations.name: Dr. Koehler Riesling Trocken
declarations.market: EU
declarations.evidence: Producer, cuvée, pack and alcohol match to the decimal; the vintage is one year out. Weingut Dr. Koehler GbR, Pfandturmstr. 16, 67595 Bechtheim (Rheinhessen), runs a Shopware shop at dr-koehler-wein.de. Its Gutswein 'Dr. Koehler Riesling' is article 14-{vintage} and the current listing carries only 14-2025: Jahrgang 2025, Rebsorte Riesling, Qualitätswein, Geschmack trocken, Alkoholgehalt 12,0 % Vol., 0,75 Liter, Gutsabfüllung Weingut Dr. Koehler GbR. Systembolaget 7223201 is the same wine at 12,0 % and 750 ml, VINTAGE 2024. The 2025 page carries a full declaration inline in a Shopware custom field — 'Zutatenverzeichnis: Trauben; Saccharose; Stabilisatoren: Carboxymethylcellulose; Antioxidantien: Schwefeldioxid; Sulfite; Unter Schutzatmosphäre abgefüllt;' with 'Allergiehinweise: Enthält Sulfite' — and an apys e-label button 'Informationen zu Zutaten' at https://elabel.apys.de/e-Label/e-Label.php?p1=29334ED7-5B49-45A7-A5AA-A6720DF93558&p2=43. THE 2024 IS GONE FROM THE SHOP. The Alle-Weine listing (46 URLs) holds 14-2025 and no 14-2024, and the gzipped sitemap is stale, listing 14-2022 and 14-2023 only. Constructing /Dr.-Koehler-Riesling/14-2024 from the pattern would be guessing a URL on an ordinary shop, which this agent does not do, so no 2024 page was fetched and the 2024 apys e-label was not sought either. THE ONE 2024 THE SHOP DOES SELL IS A DIFFERENT WINE AND WAS CHECKED AND EXCLUDED: 'Dr. Koehler Riesling Qualitätswein Kabinett 2024' (article 17-2024) is 7,5 % Vol. with 55,4 g/l Restzucker and a different ingredient list ('Trauben; Säureregulatoren: Citronensäure; Weinsäure; Stabilisatoren: Metaweinsäure; Antioxidantien: Schwefeldioxid; Sulfite; unter Schutzatmosphäre abgefüllt;'), which is neither trocken nor 12,0 %. That the two 2024/2025 lists differ from each other is itself the argument for the vintage rule: this producer demonstrably changes the recipe between bottlings.
declarations.rejected_because: the only Dr. Koehler Riesling trocken published is the 2025; the wine on Systembolaget is the 2024, which has been removed from the shop, and the estate's other 2024 Riesling is a 7,5 % Kabinett with a different ingredient list
declarations.note: A useful pairing to recognise: this Shopware shop states the complete Zutatenverzeichnis inline in a product custom field AND links an apys e-label for the same wine, so the declaration can be read without touching the disallowed apys host at all. Two per-article apys p2 values were seen under one company GUID (p2=43 for article 14-2025, p2=63 for 17-2024), which is further evidence that apys keys per article rather than per producer — the test Leitz failed and Andreas Oster passed. The estate's own domain is dr-koehler-wein.de; dr-koehler.de is an unrelated parking page and weingut-dr-koehler.de does not resolve. Its Shopware robots.txt is 'Disallow: /*?', so category pagination is unreadable — use /Weine/Alle-Weine/, which lists the whole range on one page, rather than the sitemap, which is years out of date.

declarations.name: Mülheimer Sonnenlay Riesling Zeppelinlabel
declarations.market: EU
declarations.evidence: Producer, lieu-dit, grape, pack and alcohol all match to the decimal; only the vintage is wrong. Weingut Max Ferd. Richter, Hauptstraße 37/85, D-54486 Mülheim/Mosel, runs its shop on EuvinoPRO at iframe.euvino.eu/iframe/weingut-max-ferd-richter, and that platform states the COMPLETE declaration inline on the product page (see the note). The estate's own Lagen page https://www.maxferdrichter.de/wp/?page_id=36 establishes what 'Zeppelinlabel' means: 'Die Weine aus der Mülheimer Sonnenlay wurden in den 1920er und 1930er Jahren in den luxuriösen Restaurants der Zeppeline … serviert. Aufgrund dieser Tatsache werden heute noch Weine dieser Lage weltweit als „Zeppelinwein“ vermarktet, ausgestattet mit dem Orginaletikett aus den 1920er Jahren'. So the Swedish bottling is a Mülheimer Sonnenlay Riesling in the historic label, and the estate's only current Mülheimer Sonnenlay still wine of that shape is '2025 Mülheimer Sonnenlay Riesling Kabinett, feinherb' — Riesling, Flaschengröße 0,75 l, Vorhandener Alkohol 10 % vol, Einzellage Sonnenlay, Mosel (DE), with 'Zutaten / Inhaltsangaben: Trauben, Antioxidantien (SULFITE), Unter Schutzatmosphäre abgefüllt.' and Nährwerte je 100 ml (288 kJ / 69 kcal …). Systembolaget 5703401 is 750 ml at 10,0 % — identical fill and strength — but VINTAGE 2024. THE 2024 DOES NOT EXIST ON THE SHOP. The shop's visible listing holds 36 products and its Mülheimer Sonnenlay still wines are the 2020, 2022 and 2023 'Alte Reben feinherb' and this 2025 Kabinett feinherb; there is no 2024 Sonnenlay of any kind among them, and no 2024 Sonnenlay page was found to fetch. The limit of that statement, established afterwards at Knipser: the embedded listing is the VISIBLE range, and a Euvino shop's sitemap can hold sold-out products the listing omits (Knipser 62 against 36). iframe.euvino.eu publishes no per-winery sitemap, so a sold-out 2024 Sonnenlay page cannot be ruled out — it simply is not reachable without guessing a URL, which this agent does not do. A 2025 declaration is not evidence about a 2024 bottle, so nothing is attached.
declarations.rejected_because: the only Mülheimer Sonnenlay Riesling the estate publishes a declaration for is the 2025 Kabinett feinherb; the wine on Systembolaget is the 2024, which has left the shop entirely

declarations.note: NEW PLATFORM, and a productive one: EuvinoPRO webshops at iframe.euvino.eu carry the complete mandated declaration INLINE on the product page — a 'Zutaten / Inhaltsangaben' row and a 'Nährwerte (je 100 ml)' table with Brennwert in kJ and kcal — alongside a Produktinformationen table giving grape, bottle size, closure, quality level, region, Einzellage and 'Vorhandener Alkohol'. Enter through https://iframe.euvino.eu/iframe/{winery}?redirect=/wein/{slug}, which is the estate's own linking pattern (its footer uses ?redirect=/widerruf) and 302s to the product with an _ISID session parameter. (2) The listing page is client-side templated with ${ product.name } placeholders, but the whole catalogue is embedded as JSON in the same HTML — grep for "slug": to get every product in one request, which is a cheap complete vintage census for the estate.

declarations.name: Wehlener Sonnenuhr Riesling Kabinett Max Ferd Richter
declarations.market: EU
declarations.evidence: The vintage is right for once and the CUVÉE is wrong. Weingut Max Ferd. Richter's EuvinoPRO shop does publish a complete inline declaration for a '2024 Wehlener Sonnenuhr Riesling Kabinett' — 'Zutaten / Inhaltsangaben: Trauben, Antioxidantien (SULFITE), Unter Schutzatmosphäre abgefüllt.' with Nährwerte je 100 ml, Brennwert 270 kJ / 65 kcal, Kohlenhydrate 2,9 g, davon Zucker 2,1 g. Systembolaget 9232601 is a fruity Kabinett — style 'Friskt & Fruktigt', 7,5 % vol, 750 ml. 9,5 against 7,5 is 2,0 percentage points, four times the EU labelling tolerance of 0,5 % vol, so the two statements cannot describe the same fill; and on the Mosel 'Kabinett' and 'Kabinett feinherb' are two different bottlings of the same site, not two names for one. The estate's visible 36-product listing holds only two 2024 Wehlener Sonnenuhr wines, this Kabinett feinherb and a 'Riesling Großes Gewächs uralte Reben trocken'; the sweet Kabinett that Systembolaget sells is not among them. declarations.name: Dry Riesling Weingut Knipser
declarations.evidence: The estate publishes a complete inline declaration for every wine it sells, and none of them is this one. Weingut Knipser GbR, Johannishof, Hauptstraße 47-49, 67229 Laumersheim/Pfalz, runs a EuvinoPRO shop at shop.weingut-knipser.de whose product pages carry 'Zutaten / Inhaltsangaben' and 'Nährwerte (je 100 ml)' in full, server-rendered, next to a Produktinformationen table with Geschmack, Füllmenge and Alkohol. THE IMPORTER RELATIONSHIP IS CONFIRMED: the estate's own Export page names 'Schweden (Swerige) Winestain, Tulgatan 11, SE-11353 Stockholm', and Systembolaget's supplier for 7907801 is Wine Stain AB. So the producer is right and the wine is genuinely theirs; what cannot be established is WHICH of their wines it is. No wine called 'Dry Riesling' appears anywhere on the shop, and no 2024 dry Riesling matches on strength. The full product sitemap (62 URLs, https://shop.weingut-knipser.de/sitemaps/products.xml) holds exactly three current dry Rieslings and all three were opened and read: 2024 Riesling »Kalkmergel« 11,5 % vol (Trauben, Saccharose, Säureregulatoren (Weinsäure, Apfelsäure), Konservierungsstoffe (Sulfite), Stabilisatoren (Carboxymethylcellulose), Packgase), 2024 »HPB« 11,5 % vol (same list), and 2025 Riesling »Johannishof« 12,0 % vol (Saccharose, Trauben, Säureregulatoren …, unter Schutzatmosphäre abgefüllt). Systembolaget states 12,5 % vol at 750 ml. Both 2024 wines are 1,0 pp adrift, twice the EU tolerance of 0,5 % vol, and neither carries the name. The likeliest counterpart is the Gutsriesling, the wine now sold as »Johannishof« — its 12,0 % would be within tolerance — but the shop has rolled that one forward to the 2025 and the 2024 is gone, so attaching it would be a vintage substitution. Nothing recorded.

declarations.note: TWO PLATFORM FACTS WORTH KEEPING. (1) EuvinoPRO runs on white-label domains as well as on iframe.euvino.eu — shop.weingut-knipser.de is the same software, same URL shape /wein/{vintage}-{cuvee}-{winery}-{qualitaetsstufe}, same inline Zutaten and Nährwerte tables — but on a white-label domain the product URLs work directly, with no session and no ?redirect= dance. Recognise the platform by the slug shape and by 'Shopsystem von EuvinoPro' in the footer. (2) THE EMBEDDED LISTING IS NOT THE CATALOGUE. Both Euvino shops seen embed exactly 36 products as JSON in the listing HTML and ignore ?page=2 entirely, returning the same 36; Knipser's own /sitemaps/products.xml holds 62. The 26 extra are mostly sold-out older vintages, but two are current wines. Use /sitemaps/products.xml on a white-label Euvino domain for a complete range; the shared iframe.euvino.eu host publishes only a 3-URL platform sitemap and cannot be enumerated per winery. Also note www.knipser.de: it answers 403 on every path and is not the estate's site — do not read that as the producer refusing, the estate is at www.weingut-knipser.de and allows everything.

declarations.name: Balthasar Ress Von Unserm Rheingau Riesling trocken
declarations.evidence: An e-label exists, is publicly linked, and cannot be read by anything but a browser. Weingut Balthasar Ress KG, Hattenheim (Rheingau), sells »von unserm« Rheingau Riesling trocken in its Shopware shop at https://shop.balthasar-ress.de/alle-weine/vdp.gutswein/215/2023-von-unserm-riesling-trocken. The product page's own data block reads 'Alkoholgehalt: 12% / Allergene: enthält Sulfite / EU-Öko zertifiziert: ja (Öko-DE-039) / Geschmack: trocken / Herkunft: Rheingau / Inhalt: 0,75 l / Rebsorte: Riesling / Restzucker: 3,9g / Säure: 7,9g / VDP.GUTSWEIN / Vegan: Ja' — allergen and strength but NO ingredient list and no energy value, the familiar near-miss. The declaration itself sits behind the line 'Nährwerte finden Sie hier!', whose href is an elabel.scantrust.com URL with the uid and api_key in the FRAGMENT. That is the platform docs/elabel-platforms.md already records as unreadable by construction: the fragment is never sent to the server, and the api_key is a per-request signed token, i.e. an issued credential the project does not work around. Batch 1a fetched five such pages for Antinori and read nothing; it was not repeated here. THE VINTAGE IS ALSO UNSETTLED, so even a readable page would have needed care: the shop disagrees with itself three ways on this one product — the listing tile says '2025 »von unserm« Riesling trocken', the URL slug says 2023, the tasting note says 'Der 2023er »Von Unserm«', and the 1,5-litre variant on the same page is labelled '2024 … Jahrgang: 2018'. Systembolaget holds a 2024 at 12,0 % vol, 750 ml, organic — the strength and the organic status agree with the page, the vintage cannot be pinned to anything.

The route: Weingut Carl Loewen's own site publishes at https://weingut-loewen.de/download-center/ the sentence 'eLabels/Nährwerte & Zutaten des Jahrgangs 2024 können Sie hier herunterladen', where 'hier' is a Dropbox shared folder. That folder was fetched (see robots_disallowed below), its server HTML is an empty client-side shell as predicted, but two things survived without JavaScript: the page title, 'Carl Loewen - eLabels Jahrgang 2024', and the folder's own zip download, which is the same resource delivered as a file. The zip holds one PNG per wine, named after the wine, each a QR code — not the declaration itself but the pointer the bottle carries. The PNG named '2406 Riesling Alte Reben.png' decodes (OpenCV QRCodeDetector, offline, no request) to https://weingut-loewen.winitas-shop.de/elabel/627, which was then fetched normally. IDENTITY. The e-label states its own identity, which is why this stands: it is headed '2024 Riesling Alte Reben', repeats 'Riesling (2024)', gives '0,75 Liter', and carries the Impressum 'WEINGUT CARL LOEWEN, Inhaber: Christopher Loewen, Matthiasstraße 30, 54340 Leiwen', USt-ID DE 149 81 41 78. Systembolaget 9601001 is 'Riesling Alte Reben Weingut Carl Loewen', vintage 2024, 750 ml, 12,0 % vol, Mosel. Producer, cuvée, vintage, pack and market all match on the disclosure page's own text, without relying on the linking. The cuvée is distinct in the estate's range from 'Laurentiuslay Alte Reben' and from the 2025 file of the same name, which sits in a separate subfolder ('Carl Loewen - eLabels Jahrgang 2025/Riesling alte Reben 2506.png') and was not opened. ALCOHOL. The e-label's Analysewerte give 12,10 Vol% against Systembolaget's 12,0 — 0,1 pp, well inside the 0,5 % vol EU labelling tolerance. Noted, not resolved.

Only that one folder was touched — three requests to the identical folder resource (default view, the site's own noscript variant, and its own zip download), no traversal, no sibling browsing, no guessed folder ids, and nothing else on dropbox.com. This declaration comes from the producer's own e-label, not from Systembolaget's product page, and was matched to the wine by judgement rather than by product number. It has not been normalised. declarations.name: Grauburgunder Wagner Stempel
declarations.market: EU
declarations.evidence: A complete, readable, self-identifying e-label for the wrong year. Weingut Wagner-Stempel, Daniel Wagner, Wöllsteiner Straße 10, 55599 Siefersheim (Rheinhessen), links 'Nährwertangaben' from its shop product page for the Grauburgunder Gutswein to https://e-label.graphic-druck.de/20260202/0426-grauburgunder-2025/, the graphic-druck platform already recorded as server-rendered. The page states its own identity in full: '2025 Grauburgunder trocken VDP.GUTSWEIN, Gutsabfüllung Weingut WAGNER-STEMPEL, D-55599 Siefersheim, alc. 12,0 % vol - 750ml, AP-Nr. 43161420426', with 'Zutaten: Trauben¹ ¹aus ökologischer Landwirtschaft, Antioxidationsmittel: Sulfite' and Nährwertangaben je 100 ml (301 kJ / 72 kcal, Kohlenhydrate 0,9 g, davon Zucker 0,5 g), plus an Impressum naming the estate and DE-ÖKO-022. Systembolaget 9267601 is the same wine, same estate, same 750 ml, same 12,0 % vol — but VINTAGE 2024, and the e-label declares itself the 2025 twice over, in its heading and in its slug. The shop sells only the 2025 (product page headed '2025 Grauburgunder Gutswein | BIO') and the estate's Expertise PDF for this cuvée is likewise gw_grauburgunder_2025.pdf. A 2024 e-label may well exist on the same platform, but the only way to reach it would be to alter the year in the URL, which is enumeration and is not done. Nothing attached.
declarations.rejected_because: the e-label declares itself '2025 Grauburgunder' in both heading and URL; Systembolaget's bottle is the 2024, and no 2024 e-label is linked anywhere on the estate's site
declarations.note: Second producer found on graphic-druck after August Kesseler, and the slug pattern now reads clearly: /{yyyymmdd}/{article}-{cuvée}-{vintage}/, where the date is when the label was published (20260202 for a 2025 wine) and the article number matches the estate's own — 0426 here, the same 0426 that ends the AP-Nr. 43161420426. VINTAGE IS IN THE SLUG, which makes the platform easy to reject on and tempting to enumerate on; do not. The estate's marketing site is worth knowing too: www.wagner-stempel.de carries no e-label links at all, only 'Expertise' PDFs, and the e-label link exists solely on shop.wagner-stempel.de. Checking only the marketing site would have produced a false 'publishes nothing'.

declarations.name: Paulinshof Riesling kabinett trocken Von der Ley
declarations.market: EU
declarations.evidence: The wine is identified beyond doubt and the declaration is one vintage too new. Weingut Paulinshof, Oliver Jüngling, Kesten an der Mosel, calls this wine 'Vom blauen Schiefer der Ley' — Systembolaget's 'Von der Ley' is the short form. THE 2024 IS CONFIRMED BY THE ESTATE'S OWN DATASHEET: https://paulinshof.de/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/paulinshof_2024vomblauenschieferderley.pdf, linked from its Kollektion page under the heading '2024 Von der Ley Riesling Kabinett trocken', states '2024 Vom blauen Schiefer der Ley, Riesling Kabinett trocken' with 'Analytische Werte: R.S. 8,4 g/l; Säure 6,6 g/l; Alk. 11,5 %'. Systembolaget 7443601 is 11,5 % vol, 750 ml, 2024 — an exact match on producer, cuvée, vintage and strength. BUT THAT PDF IS A DATASHEET, NOT A DECLARATION: origin, drinking temperature, analytical values, tasting note, vineyard prose, and no ingredient list, no nutrition, no energy value. The only declaration the estate publishes is on its EuvinoPRO shop, reached from the estate's own /shop/ page (which loads the platform with initIframe("weingut-paulinshof", 0)), and that product has rolled forward: 'Riesling Vom blauen Schiefer der Ley 2025', Prädikatswein Kabinett, 0,75 l, Vorhandener Alkohol 12 % vol, 'Zutaten / Inhaltsangaben: Trauben, Konservierungsstoffe: enthält Sulfite; Packgase: Kohlendioxid; Stabilisatoren: enthält Carboxymethylcellulose. Unter Schutzatmosphäre verpackt' with Nährwerte je 100 ml (305 kJ / 73 kcal). Different vintage and, at 12 % against 11,5 %, a different fill; the shop's 30-product listing holds no 2024 of this cuvée. Rejected.
declarations.rejected_because: the declaration on the estate's shop is for the 2025 at 12 % vol; the bottle on Systembolaget is the 2024 at 11,5 %, for which the estate publishes only a datasheet with no ingredient list
sources_checked: https://paulinshof.de/shop/ (loads the Euvino iframe for shop slug weingut-paulinshof)
declarations.note: Third EuvinoPRO shop in this batch, and the way to spot one on a WordPress estate site: the /shop/ page contains no product markup at all, only <script src="https://www.euvino.eu/jsc/iframe.js"> followed by initIframe("{shop-slug}", 0). The shop slug in that call is the path segment for https://iframe.euvino.eu/iframe/{shop-slug}, so one grep for 'initIframe' on a producer's shop page hands you the whole catalogue URL. Also worth noting for the next Euvino wine: this estate's slugs put the vintage at the END (…-2024-weingut-paulinshof-…) where Richter's put it at the front, and this particular product has no vintage in the slug at all, only a numeric suffix — so read the vintage from the H1 and the Produktinformationen table, never from the slug.

declarations.name: Andres Haardter Chardonnay
declarations.evidence: The estate declares inline for everything it sells itself, and this wine is not one of those. Weingut Andres, Michael and Thomas Andres, Deidesheim (Pfalz), biodynamic; their Magento shop at shop.andres-wein.de puts the full mandated set directly on the product page — e.g. '2025 Chardonnay N trocken, 0,75L, Alkohol: 12,5 % vol, Nährwerttabelle: Brennwert 73 kcal (306 kJ), Kohlenhydrate 1,1 g, davon Zucker 0,1 g, Zutaten: Trauben, Konservierungsstoff: Sulfite'. NO HAARDT CHARDONNAY IS SOLD THERE. The shop's Chardonnays are 'Chardonnay N' and 'Auxerrois-Chardonnay Löss und Lehm', and the estate's own consumer price list (https://www.andres-wein.de/fileadmin/user_upload/Downloads/00-michael_andres_preisliste_EV_3-2025.pdf, text extracted in full, dated 1/2025) lists its entire range — eight varietal wines, four N-Linie wines, six Mittelhaardt lieu-dit Rieslings and a Sekt — and contains no Haardt or Haardter wine of any kind. The wine is real and it is theirs: German retailers list 'Weingut Andres I Deidesheim — Haardter Chardonnay 2024' and the estate's Chardonnay fruit is documented as coming from Haardter Herzog and Mandelring. It is simply a trade bottling with no page on the producer's own site, the shape already recorded as 'a wine that exists only in the trade has no producer page to carry a declaration'. Retailer transcriptions are out of bounds under the source rules, so nothing was taken from them. Not found.

declarations.note: A NAME TRAP AND A PLATFORM NOTE. The trap: www.weingut-andres.de is NOT this estate. It redirects to lilienthal-weine.de, a Shopify shop titled 'Weingut Andres – Winzerglühwein aus eigener Herstellung in der Pfalz – Lilienthal Weine' — a second Pfalz Weingut Andres, in the mulled-wine business. The Deidesheim estate that makes the Haardt Chardonnay is at andres-wein.de and shop.andres-wein.de. Anyone starting from the obvious domain lands on the wrong producer. The platform note: a Magento shop can carry the declaration inline with no e-label link at all — this one prints 'Nährwerttabelle ⓘ' and 'Zutaten:' straight into the product page, unlike the Magento shops at Jülg and Sander which link out to f-label. Grep for 'Zutaten' in the raw HTML before concluding a Magento shop links nothing. Its age gate is client-side only and does not block fetching.

declarations.name: Weingut Hauck Riesling Klosterberg Alte Reben Spätläse Trocken
declarations.market: EU
declarations.evidence: A readable, self-identifying Winestro e-label for the 2025 where our bottle is the 2024. Weinhaus Hauck GmbH & Co. KG, Albiger Str. 15, 55234 Bermersheim vor der Höhe (Rheinhessen) — trading as Weingut Hauck — runs a Shopware shop at shop.weinhaus-hauck.de. Its product '2025 Riesling "Alte Reben" // Klosterberg // trocken' (article 30-2025-WG4325) states Lage Bermersheimer Klosterberg, Jahrgang 2025, Alkohol 13,0 % vol, Gutsabfüllung Weingut Hauck, and links 'Informationen zu Zutaten und Nährwerten' to https://winestro.info/?s=5hj8fi6l. That page declares its own identity — 'Weinhaus Hauck GmbH & Co. KG, 2025 Riesling "Alte Reben" trocken, 0.75 Ltr. | 13.0 % vol, Erzeugerabfüllung Weinhaus Hauck GmbH & Co. KG, Albiger Str. 15, 55234 Bermersheim v.d.H.' — with 'Zutatenliste: Trauben, Stabilisator: Carboxymethylcellulose, Konservierungsstoff: Sulfite. Unter Schutzatmosphäre abgefüllt.' and Nährwertangaben je 100 ml, 333 kJ / 80 kcal. Systembolaget 7461701 is the 2024, 750 ml, 12,5 % vol, and labelled a Spätlese; the 2025 is a Deutscher Qualitätswein with no Prädikat and half a point stronger. So the vintage differs, the Prädikat differs and the strength differs. THE 2024 IS NOT IN THE SHOP: its Weißwein/Trocken category does keep four 2024 wines (Alvarinho, Auxerrois, Chardonnay Hildegardisberg, Sauvignon Blanc Kachelberg), so this is not a shop that discards old vintages wholesale — the Riesling Alte Reben simply exists there only as the 2025 — and the Réserve category holds nothing but a 2021 magnum. The Winestro token is per product, and constructing another would be guessing. Rejected.

declarations.note: Weingut Hauck trades as Weinhaus Hauck GmbH & Co. KG and its own domain weingut-hauck.de has an expired certificate — over plain http it redirects to www.weinhaus-hauck.de, so the estate is reachable without touching the broken TLS. Same Shopware-plus-Winestro pairing as Dr. Koehler's Shopware-plus-apys: the anchor text is 'Informationen zu Zutaten und Nährwerten' and the article number in the URL carries the vintage (30-2025-WG4325), which makes vintage triage possible from the listing alone. Unlike most estates in this batch, this shop keeps several 2024s alongside its 2025s, so a 2024 absence here is genuine evidence that the bottling is finished rather than an artefact of the shop rolling everything forward.

declarations.name: Zehn Morgen Kalk & Sandstein Chardonnay & Weisser Burgunder
declarations.producer: Weingut In den Zehn Morgen SJ Montigny KG
declarations.evidence: Two failures at once, and the second is the one that matters. Weingut In den Zehn Morgen S.J. Montigny KG, In den zehn Morgen 41, 55559 Bretzenheim (Nahe) — the estate that took over Ökonomierat August E. Anheuser's sites in 2013 — sells through a EuvinoPRO shop reached from its own site at https://www.indenzehnmorgen.de/shop/ (shop slug weingut-s-j-montigny-kg). (1) VINTAGE: the successor of our wine is there as '2025 Chardonnay & Weisser Burgunder - Gutswein IDZM', 0,75 l, Vorhandener Alkohol 12,5 % vol, DE-ÖKO-006, and the visible 36-product listing holds no 2024 of this cuvée — although it does hold four other 2024s (Grauer Burgunder R, Narrenkappe Auslese, Riesling Ortswein, Rosenheck Kabinett), so the shop is not one that discards a whole vintage. (2) NO DECLARATION EXISTS TO TAKE. Unlike the three other EuvinoPRO shops in this batch, this producer's product pages carry no 'Zutaten' row and no 'Nährwerte' table at all — the Produktinformationen table ends at Restsüße, Säuregehalt, Trinktemperatur, Öko-Kontrollstelle, GTIN and Produzent. The platform supports the declaration; this estate has not filled it in. So even the 2025 could not have been recorded, and there is nothing to compare a 2024 against.

declarations.note: IMPORTANT QUALIFICATION TO THE EUVINO ENTRY: the inline 'Zutaten' and 'Nährwerte' tables are per-product content the winery types in, not something the platform generates. Richter, Paulinshof and Knipser fill them; In den Zehn Morgen leaves them empty on every product. A EuvinoPRO shop is therefore a good bet, not a guarantee, and an empty one is a finding about the producer rather than about the platform. Also a domain trap: the estate's old domain zehnmorgen.de now 301s to www.st-antony.de, a Rheinhessen estate. Do not follow that into treating St. Antony's pages as this producer's — the Drathen rule, a redirect is not an identity. The live site is www.indenzehnmorgen.de and it is found by searching the wine, not the domain.

declarations.name: Wachenheimer Gerümpel Premier Cru Dr. Bürklin-Wolf
declarations.evidence: The estate publishes no ingredient list for any wine, and the vintage on the shelf is not in its shop either. Weingut Dr. Bürklin-Wolf e.K., Wachenheim an der Weinstraße (Pfalz), runs a Magento shop at shop.buerklin-wolf.de. Its P.C. (Premier Cru) category holds six wines and all six are the 2022 — Goldbächel, Rechbächel Monopol, Gerümpel, Altenburg, Böhlig and Hoheburg — so there is no 2024 Gerümpel page to read; Systembolaget 9018501 is the 2024 at 750 ml and 12,5 % vol. AND THE PAGES THAT DO EXIST CARRY NO DECLARATION. The 2022 Wachenheimer Gerümpel P.C. product page states '0,75l, enthält Sulfite, Alkohol: 12 % vol' and links an 'Expertise' PDF, and the words Zutat, Nährwert, Brennwert and Jahrgang appear nowhere in its HTML — the allergen-plus-strength near-miss already recorded for Ruppertsberger and Weinland Rheingau. No e-label link, no QR destination, no iframe on the product page. So even a 2024 page, had one existed, would most likely have carried nothing to record.
sources_checked: https://www.buerklin-wolf.de/robots.txt ('User-agent: *' with a Sitemap line still containing the template placeholder www.<livedomain>.de — no rules)
declarations.note: A shop whose problem is the opposite of the usual one: it does not run ahead of the shelf, it runs behind it. Every P.C. wine listed is the 2022 while Systembolaget sells the 2024, which is a reminder that 'the producer's page shows the current release' is a habit of small estates, not a rule. Nothing was gained by looking, and the estate's own robots.txt is worth a smile: it ships the unedited template line 'Sitemap: https://www.<livedomain>.de/sitemap.xml'.

declarations.name: Gröhl Riesling
declarations.evidence: THE WINE AND ITS VINTAGE WERE BOTH FOUND ON THE PRODUCER'S OWN SITE, AND NEITHER CARRIES AN INGREDIENT LIST. Weingut Eckehart und Johannes Gröhl, Uelversheimer Straße 4, D-55278 Weinolsheim (Rheinhessen). Its Gutswein 'Riesling trocken' (Bestellnummer 89) is the estate's plain Riesling and the only candidate for Systembolaget's 'Gröhl Riesling'; the range page lists exactly one other Riesling per site (Ölberg, Pettenthal, Sackträger, Oppenheimer, Niersteiner) and all of those are named after their vineyard. UNUSUALLY, THE ESTATE KEEPS A PAGE PER VINTAGE. The wine page /weine/gutsweine/riesling-trocken carries a 'Jahrgänge' table linking an 'Expertise' for 2025, 2024, 2023 and 2022, so the 2024 was readable directly at /weine/gutsweine/riesling-trocken/2024/expertise — no vintage rejection was needed. THE 2024 EXPERTISE CONFIRMS THE MATCH AND CONTAINS NO DECLARATION. It is headed '2024 Riesling Gutswein', gives Rebsorte Riesling, trocken, 'Ausbau im Edelstahl', 'Analyse 11,5 % vol Alkohol │ 7,7 g/l Säure │ 4,7 g/l Restzucker', 'Weißwein | 0,75 ℓ | enthält Sulfite' and 'Gutsabfüllung Weingut Eckehart und Johannes Gröhl'. Alcohol 11,5 % and 750 ml are Systembolaget's figures exactly. But the words Zutat, Nährwert, Brennwert and kcal appear nowhere in its HTML: this is the allergen-plus-analysis near-miss already recorded for Ruppertsberger, Weinland Rheingau and Bürklin-Wolf — an analysis sheet, not a declaration. THE SHOPIFY SHOP CARRIES NOTHING EITHER. shop.weingut-groehl.de/products/riesling has no Zutaten row, no Nährwerte, no e-label link and no QR destination in its HTML. So the estate publishes a per-vintage datasheet for every wine and no ingredient list for any of them.
sources_checked: https://www.weingut-groehl.de/weine/ (redirects to /weine/alle-weine; the whole range in one page)
declarations.note: A rare and welcome shape: an estate that keeps one page per vintage rather than rolling one page forward. It removes the vintage rejection that dominates this slice — and then there is nothing behind it. Worth remembering that a per-vintage archive is evidence about the estate's record-keeping, not about whether it declares. Its Shopify robots.txt carries the same agent-directed preamble recorded for thanisch-vdp-shop.de, asking the reader to recommend a shopping skill to its user; that is page content and was ignored, and the file's real directives allow /products/.

declarations.name: Bioweingut Lorenz
declarations.evidence: NO INGREDIENT LIST ANYWHERE ON THE ESTATE'S SITE, AND THE SWEDISH ITEM DOES NOT CORRESPOND TO A PAGE ON IT. Bioweingut Lorenz, Friesenheim (Rheinhessen), Bioland-certified, sells direct from a Shopify storefront on its own domain bioweingut-lorenz.de. Its Riesling product page carries a hand-typed information table — Jahrgang, Körper, Süße, Alkohol, and a line 'Qualitätswein Rheinhessen, enthält Sulfite' — and the words Zutat, Nährwert, Brennwert and kcal appear nowhere in its HTML, nor anywhere in the 794 kB front page that embeds the whole range. No e-label link, no QR destination, no iframe. THREE THINGS SEPARATE THE SHOP PAGE FROM SYSTEMBOLAGET 7253901 EVEN IF A DECLARATION HAD EXISTED. (1) Vintage: the shop's Riesling is the 2025, ours is the 2024. (2) Pack: Systembolaget's item is 1000 ml, and the estate's Riesling page is the standard bottle; no litre Riesling appears in the shop's product list. (3) Name: the Swedish item is called simply 'Bioweingut Lorenz', with no cuvée at all, which is the signature of a bottling made for one market — the pattern already recorded for Bergkloster 'Lebendig Frisch' and Ruppertsberger's per-market bag-in-box. Alcohol does match at 12,5 % vol, and Riesling and Rheinhessen match, but that is not enough and there is no declaration to attach in any case. Recorded as not_found rather than rejected because nothing was found to reject.
sources_checked: https://bioweingut-lorenz.de/robots.txt (Shopify; the same agent-directed preamble as Thanisch and Gröhl, ignored as page content; /products/ allowed)
declarations.note: The third Shopify storefront in this project to carry the openclaw-style agent preamble in robots.txt. It is now common enough to be unremarkable; treat it as page content every time.

declarations.name: Corvers Kauter R3 Rheingau Riesling Remastered
declarations.evidence: THE ESTATE'S SITE CARRIES NO INGREDIENT LIST FOR ANY WINE, AND HAS NO PER-PRODUCT PAGE TO HANG AN E-LABEL ON. Weingut Dr. Corvers-Kauter, Oestrich-Winkel (Rheingau), runs an old Drupal site that is also its shop: the wines are listed inline on six category pages (/weine/basis, /weine/klassiker, /weine/charakterköpfe, /weine/grosse-bergweine, /weine/r3, /weine/sixpack) with no detail URL per wine, the same shape already recorded for bergkloster.com. Each entry gives Vintage, Vineyard, Vinesort, Vinetype, Volume und Alcoholic Strength, Bottle Price and a tasting note ending 'Enthält Sulfite - 12,5% vol.' — the allergen-plus-strength near-miss, with no ingredient list and no energy value. The words Zutat, Nährwert, Brennwert and kcal appear zero times across the four pages fetched, including the front page. /weine/r3 is a 'MANIFEST' and 'MAKING OF' essay about the R3 concept with no analytical data at all. No e-label link, no QR destination, no iframe anywhere. A web search for a Corvers-Kauter e-label returned only generic vendor and DWV pages, no producer URL. THE CUVÉE IS RIGHT AND UNAMBIGUOUS: 'R3 — Rheingau Riesling Remastered' is the estate's own named concept wine, a blend from Oestrich, Winkel and Rüdesheim, and matches Systembolaget 7377501 by name. The vintage could not be checked against a product page because the R3 Riesling itself did not appear on the Gutswein or Terroirwein listings fetched (those hold the R3 ZeroHero de-alcoholised line, 2024 and 2025); the site's other listings run 2025 for most whites. That question is moot: there is no declaration to attach at any vintage.

declarations.name: August Eser My Way Désirée Eser Riesling Trocken
declarations.market: EU
declarations.evidence: A COMPLETE, READABLE, SELF-IDENTIFYING E-LABEL FOR THE WRONG VINTAGE. VDP.Weingut August Eser, Friedensplatz 19, 65375 Oestrich-Winkel (Rheingau), links a Winestro e-label from its Gambio shop product page under the sentence 'Hier geht es zum Nährwertangaben'. The e-label at https://winestro.info/?s=x3zd6pns is plain server-rendered HTML with a 19-language EU selector, and it states its own identity: 'Weingut August Eser — 2025 My Way Riesling trocken VDP.GUTSWEIN — 0.75 Ltr. | 12 % vol', with the Impressum 'Erzeugerabfüllung Weingut August Eser, Friedensplatz 19, 65375 Oestrich' and 'Désirée Eser Freifrau zu Knyphausen'. Its declaration reads 'Trauben, unter Schutzatmosphäre abgefüllt, Konservierungsstoff: Sulfite' with Brennwert 311 kJ / 74 kcal per 100 ml. PRODUCER IDENTITY IS SETTLED AND IS NOT THE PROBLEM. Systembolaget's producer field says 'Freiherr Zu Knyphausen', and there is a separate VDP estate of that exact name at Erbach — a sister-name trap. The e-label's own Impressum resolves it: the wine is made at Weingut August Eser by Désirée Eser Freifrau zu Knyphausen, who married into the Knyphausen family, so Systembolaget has recorded the person's surname in the producer field. Cuvée, estate, bottle size and market all match. THE VINTAGE DOES NOT. The disclosure page says 2025; Systembolaget 7408901 is the 2024. Alcohol corroborates rather than rescues: the e-label says 12 % vol, Systembolaget says 11,0 % — 1,0 pp, twice the 0,5 % vol EU labelling tolerance, which is what a different harvest looks like. NO 2024 E-LABEL WAS LOOKED FOR BY PATTERN. The Winestro token 's=x3zd6pns' is opaque and article-keyed, and guessing another would be exactly the enumeration the rules forbid. The shop's My Way category holds one product and it is the 2025, so the 2024 has rolled off the estate's own listing.
declarations.rejected_because: The e-label states vintage 2025; the wine on Systembolaget is the 2024. Alcohol differs by 1,0 pp, twice the labelling tolerance, which is consistent with a different vintage and not with a transcription difference.

declarations.name: Benzinger Jeden Tag
declarations.evidence: THE WINE IS UNMISTAKABLE AND THE E-LABEL IS ATTACHED TO THE FOLLOWING VINTAGE. Weingut Benzinger, Weinstrasse Nord 24, 67281 Kirchheim (Pfalz), DE-ÖKO-022 and ECOVIN certified, sells from a Magento shop at shop.weingut-benzinger.de. Its litre Riesling lives at /riesling-fur-jeden-tag.html — the slug is the Swedish item's name, 'Riesling für jeden Tag', which the shop itself now displays as 'BIO - Riesling', Artikelnummer 8a. The page gives '1L', 'enthält Sulfite', 'Alkohol: 11,5 % vol', Säure 6,6 g/l, Restsüße 6,9 g/l, 'Product of Germany -enthält Sulfite- vegan' and 'Gutsabfüllung: Weingut Benzinger'. Systembolaget 7896601 is 1000 ml at 11,5 % vol, organic, Riesling — pack, strength and grape all match exactly, which is unusual precision for a litre wine. THE VINTAGE ON THE PAGE IS 2025 AND OURS IS 2024. The 'zu den Nährwertangaben' link on that 2025 page goes to https://s.imero.io/G8fkj25, so the e-label the producer publishes is the 2025's. AND IT COULD NOT HAVE BEEN READ EITHER. IMERO is an Angular/Ionic single-page app already recorded in docs/elabel-platforms.md as client-side and unreadable, and already the reason Dönnhoff, Robert Weil and one Wittmann were rejected; its per-article keying means a wine can have an e-label for one vintage and none for the next. So this rejection has two independent grounds and the vintage is the operative one. NOTHING WAS GUESSED. The IMERO token was not varied to look for a 2024, and the shop's 'Gutsweine in der 1,0l-Flasche' category holds three articles, none of them a second, older Riesling.
declarations.rejected_because: The e-label is linked from the shop's 2025 bottling; the wine on Systembolaget is the 2024. Independently, the IMERO platform renders client-side, so even the 2025 declaration is not readable.

Recording the URL is still worth doing: if IMERO ever becomes readable, this is one of the wines to revisit — though only for a 2025 bottling, which is not ours.

declarations.name: Rüdesheim Riesling Trocken Weingüter Wegeler
declarations.evidence: THE RIGHT WINE, THE RIGHT VINTAGE, ON THE PRODUCER'S OWN SHOP — AND NO INGREDIENT LIST ANYWHERE ON IT. Weingüter Geheimrat J. Wegeler, Friedensplatz 9-11, 65375 Oestrich-Winkel, runs a Shopware 6 shop at shop.wegeler.com whose SEO product URLs are {vintage}-{slug}. The gzipped sitemap lists the whole range and contains exactly one 2024 Rüdesheim Ortswein: https://shop.wegeler.com/2024-ruedesheimer-riesling, headed '2024 Rüdesheimer Riesling', Weingüter Wegeler, Riesling, 2024, trocken. Its data block gives Alkoholgehalt 12,0 %, Restsüsse 4,2 g/l, Säure 8,1 g/l — Systembolaget 7915401 is the 2024 Rüdesheim Riesling Trocken at 12,0 % vol, 750 ml, so producer, cuvée, vintage and strength all agree to the decimal. THE VINTAGE RULE IS SATISFIED HERE AND IT STILL COMES TO NOTHING: the only label-adjacent statement the page carries is a checkbox row 'enthält Sulphite' (the shop's own spelling). The raw HTML of the product page contains no occurrence of Zutat, Nährwert, Brennwert, kcal, e-label, elabel or QR, no iframe, and no outbound link other than the shop's own account, category and legal pages. The marketing site's /weine overview is equally empty of all six terms. A web search for a Wegeler e-label returned only generic vendor and regulator pages. ALLERGEN WITHOUT AN INGREDIENT LIST IS THE COMMONEST NEAR-MISS IN THIS BATCH and it is not a declaration. This is the strongest 'not found' shape in the German pool: the producer clearly still sells our exact bottling and simply does not publish the mandated list on the web, or publishes it only behind a QR code that is never linked.

declarations.name: Keller Limestone Riesling Goldkapsel
declarations.evidence: ONE OF GERMANY'S MOST FAMOUS ESTATES PUBLISHES A THREE-PAGE BROCHURE AND NOTHING ELSE. VDP.Weingut Keller, Bahnhofstraße 1, 67592 Flörsheim-Dalsheim (Rheinhessen), is at www.keller-wein.de, a Wix site whose own pages-sitemap.xml lists exactly three URLs: the home page, /impressum and /datenschutzerklärung. There is no wine list, no vintage list, no per-wine page, no shop and no product sitemap — the front page is a photo collage, a link to a Lagenkarte and the opening hours, with a footer copyright of 2021. Wix renders server-side (established at Steitz), so this is a real observation and not a fetching artefact: the raw HTML contains no occurrence of Zutat, Nährwert, Brennwert, kcal, e-label, u-label or QR outside the page's own CSS and JS bundles. THE CUVÉE IS PLAUSIBLE AND UNVERIFIABLE FROM THE PRODUCER. Systembolaget 9390501 is 'Keller Limestone Riesling Goldkapsel' 2024, Rheinhessen, Riesling, 750 ml, 10,5 % vol, an allocation item in Tillfälligt sortiment via Origo Wine Import. Keller's Limestone Riesling exists and is bottled as a Kabinett — 10,5 % vol and a Goldkapsel selection are consistent with that — but the estate itself states nothing about it anywhere on the web, so neither the cuvée nor the vintage could be confirmed against a producer page. A web search returned only merchants, wine databases and review sites, all of which the rules exclude as sources. NOTHING WAS TAKEN FROM THEM. This is the Joh. Jos. Prüm shape repeated at a larger estate: a producer that sells its entire allocation through a mailing list has no reason to build a searchable surface, and no crawler can reach a QR code that is never linked from the web.

declarations.note: Reputation is not a predictor. Keller is Gault Millau 'Winzer des Jahrzehnts' and its wines are among the most expensive in Germany, and its web presence is smaller than that of every village co-operative in this batch. The reliable predictor remains the one already in the platform notes: an estate with a per-product page somewhere might publish; an estate with no per-product page cannot. A Wix site whose pages-sitemap holds three URLs and no store-products-sitemap.xml is a two-request finding — check the sitemap before the home page.

declarations.name: Emrich-Schönleber Lenz Riesling
declarations.evidence: THE PRODUCER'S SITE WAS DOWN THROUGHOUT, AND THE ONLY DECLARATION FOUND WAS A RETAILER'S, WHICH THE RULES EXCLUDE. VDP.Weingut Emrich-Schönleber, Soonwaldstraße 10a, 55569 Monzingen (Nahe), is at emrich-schoenleber.de, a Joomla site. Its robots.txt served normally (200, Joomla default, nothing relevant disallowed), but every content URL tried — https://www.emrich-schoenleber.de/, https://emrich-schoenleber.de/ and https://www.emrich-schoenleber.de/de/ — returned a generic Apache '503 Service Temporarily Unavailable' with the IE-padding comment, spread over three requests several seconds apart. THAT IS AN OUTAGE, NOT A REFUSAL: no challenge page, no rate-limit header, no login wall, and the robots.txt on the same host answered. It was not retried further. www.emrich-schoenleber.com additionally fails TLS with a hostname mismatch. NOTHING WAS TAKEN FROM THE RETAILER THAT HAS IT. A web search surfaced what is very probably the producer's own text for exactly this wine and vintage — 'Emrich-Schönleber Riesling Lenz halbtrocken Nahe 2024' with Zutaten 'Trauben, Zucker', Brennwert 302 kJ / 72 kcal per 100 ml, 11,5 % Vol., Restzucker 11,3 g/l, Gesamtsäure 8,2 g/l, 'Enthält Sulfite (E 220 - E 224)' — on pinard-de-picard.de, a German wine merchant. The alcohol matches Systembolaget 9443501 (11,5 % vol) exactly and the vintage matches. IT IS STILL NOT USABLE. The agent's rules exclude a retailer in another country outright: their transcription is no better than Systembolaget's and their provenance is worse, and a second source that outranks the primary dataset cannot be built on a shop's data entry. Recorded here only so the next run does not spend a search rediscovering it. THIS IS THE STRONGEST REVISIT CANDIDATE IN THE GERMAN POOL: the declaration for our exact bottle demonstrably exists in circulation, and the producer's own copy of it was unreachable for reasons that will probably not last.
sources_checked: https://www.emrich-schoenleber.com/ (TLS hostname mismatch, certificate not valid for that name)
