declarations.fetch_result: HTTP 503 on every content URL, three requests, no retry loop. Transient server error, not a technological refusal.
declarations.note: Worth separating two things the report should not blur. A 503 is not a bot challenge and not a Disallow: it is the host failing, and the correct handling is to record not_found, say so, and move on — the wine is a candidate for a later run, not a closed question. And the retailer near-miss is the sharpest illustration yet of why the source rules matter: the text is right there, it matches on vintage and alcohol, and taking it would put a shop's transcription above Systembolaget's in a file that outranks the primary dataset. That is exactly the silent corruption the project forbids.

declarations.name: Even & Odd Riesling
declarations.evidence: THE PRODUCER WAS IDENTIFIED, AND THE PRODUCER SAYS IN SO MANY WORDS THAT THIS WINE HAS NO PAGE. Systembolaget 7352301 carries the importer in the producer field ('Spring Wine & Spirits', supplier Spendrups). The agency's own product page, https://springwine.se/produkter/vin/vitt/even-odd-riesling/, names the estate outright in a 'Producent' field: WEINGUT MEHRLEIN, Rheingau, Riesling 100 %. That is an importer's attribution rather than the producer's own statement, so it settles which estate to look at and nothing more — no declaration was taken from it. WEINGUT MEHRLEIN PUBLISHES NO PRODUCT PAGES AT ALL, AND EXPLAINS WHY. weingut-mehrlein.de is a seven-page static HTML brochure (weingut, produktion, aktuelles, weine, venture, eco-step, kontakt) with no shop, no wine list and no per-wine URL; there is no robots.txt (404). Its /weine.html says the estate is a Rheingau Riesling specialist working with Handelspartner and — verbatim — 'Da die Weine für unsere Partner exklusiv vinifiziert werden, finden Sie im Weingut meist nicht den gleichen Wein, jedoch stets die gleich hohe Qualität!' A house that vinifies each cuvée exclusively for a trade partner has, by its own account, no 'Even & Odd' in its own range to hang an e-label on. The raw HTML of /weine.html contains no occurrence of Zutat, Nährwert, Brennwert, kcal, e-label or QR. This is the pattern already named in docs/elabel-platforms.md — a wine that exists only on the Swedish shelf has no producer page to carry a declaration — here confirmed by the producer's own words rather than inferred from an absence.

declarations.note: Worth carrying forward: when Systembolaget's producer field holds a Swedish importer, the importer's own agency site often names the estate in a 'Producent' field, and that is a cheap way to convert an unidentifiable item into a real producer to probe. It converted this one in two requests. What it converted it into was a dead end, but a documented dead end — Mehrlein's own text about exclusive vinification for trade partners is the clearest statement in this whole batch of why private-label bottlings cannot be traced to a producer declaration.

declarations.name: Pride Riesling Fab&Fruity
declarations.evidence: AN IMPORTER'S OWN BRAND WHOSE PRODUCER COULD NOT BE ESTABLISHED, SO NOTHING WAS LOOKED FOR AND NOTHING WAS GUESSED. Systembolaget records the producer as 'Solera Sweden AB', which is the Swedish importer (part of Royal Unibrew), not an estate. Solera's site lists 21 producers by name across its whole portfolio and not one is a Rheingau estate or a German Riesling house; the closest German names on that list are ZGM and Weinhaus, both large private-label bottlers, and attributing a Rheingau Riesling to either on that basis would be precisely the sister-estate guess the matching rules forbid. Its B2B webshop is the only place the item could be looked up, and the shop's own robots.txt disallows */catalogsearch/ and every /*?q= query, so it cannot be searched within the directives; the /se_sv/produkter listing returns the category tree but no product grid in the server HTML. The Springwine trick that worked one wine earlier in this batch — an importer page naming the estate in a 'Producent' field — has no counterpart here. WITHOUT AN IDENTIFIED PRODUCER THERE IS NO PAGE TO CHECK AGAINST AND NO IDENTITY TEST TO RUN. This is recorded as not found on the strict reading: not that no declaration exists, but that the four matching rules cannot even be attempted. THE ITEM HERE IS 'Pride Riesling Fab&Fruity' 2024, Rheingau, Riesling, 750 ml, 12,0 % vol, Ordervaror. The name appears nowhere outside Swedish retail aggregators, which is the signature of a Swedish-market own label.

declarations.evidence: THE IMPORTER'S SITE WAS SEARCHED PROPERLY AND THE WINE IS NOT ON IT. A CLOUDFLARE MANAGED CHALLENGE, WHICH IS A REFUSAL AND STOPS THE FETCH. Maison M. Chapoutier, Tain-l'Hermitage, is the producer for all four Swedish wines and the identity is not in doubt — Systembolaget's supplier is Lively Wines Sweden AB and the producer field names Chapoutier directly. The site's robots.txt is served normally and is permissive: it disallows only the login, password-reset and cart paths and the ?order= sort parameter, and it advertises four locale sitemaps. But every content URL behind it answers HTTP 403 with the Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' interstitial — a managed challenge carrying a per-request __cf_chl_tk token and a challenge-platform script. Two requests were made (the fr sitemap the robots.txt itself names, and the fr home page) and both were challenged; no third was made and nothing was attempted to get around it. Under this project's rules a bot challenge is a technological measure and is absolute, unlike robots.txt, so the e-label exception does not reach it and the crawl stopped there. NO ALTERNATIVE HOST EXISTS TO TRY. Chapoutier's Roussillon estate Domaine de Bila-Haut and its Pays d'Oc Marius range are both published under www.chapoutier.com; domainedebilahaut.com, bilahaut.com, www.bila-haut.com, elabel.chapoutier.com and label.chapoutier.com do not resolve, and a web search surfaced no e-label URL for the house. Recorded as not found on the strict reading: the four matching rules could not be attempted at all. Whether Chapoutier publishes a declaration is unknown and unknowable from here without stepping over the challenge.

declarations.evidence: THE HOUSE'S WHOLE SHOPIFY CATALOGUE WAS CHECKED AND IT PUBLISHES NO INGREDIENT LIST ANYWHERE. Gerard Bertrand SA, Narbonne, is the producer and Systembolaget's supplier is Ward Wines AB; the producer field is the estate, not a brand or an importer, so no identification step was needed. The shop is the best-structured French site in this batch: a Shopify storefront whose product sitemap holds 581 URLs, one per cuvee per vintage per format, so the vintage question is answerable from the sitemap alone. Two product pages were fetched and the raw HTML of both was grepped for 'ingredient', 'nutrition', 'etiquette', 'allergene', 'energetique', 'kcal', 'sulfite', 'u-label' and 'e-label': ZERO MATCHES IN EITHER, on nearly 400 kB and 420 kB of HTML respectively. The pages sitemap holds 212 pages and none of them is an ingredient, nutrition or e-label page. The metaobject sitemap — the Shopify feature a house of this size would most naturally use for per-wine e-labels — holds 73 objects that are eleven estate pages, nine distributor pages and fifty-three cocktail and food recipes. THE ONE DOCUMENT THAT LOOKS LIKE A DECLARATION IS NOT ONE. Each product links a PDF datasheet on the Shopify CDN; the Clairette's was fetched and its text extracted in full, and it carries presentation, vinification, tasting notes and grape variety, no ingredient list, no nutrition table, and not even a vintage. That is the same near-miss shape recorded for Von Winning and Schloss Johannisberg in the German batch. The FR (EU) storefront was used throughout; the .co.uk and .de storefronts are separate hosts and were not fetched. THIS WINE'S OWN PAGE, AT OUR OWN VINTAGE AND PACK, EXISTS: /products/art-de-vivre-vin-blanc-clairette-du-languedoc-adissan-75cl-2024-vin-blanc-sucre, SKU 827001, the Art de Vivre AOP Clairette du Languedoc Adissan, 75 cl, 2024 — matching Systembolaget 7293201 (750 ml, 2024) on cuvee, vintage and pack. The vintage rule is satisfied and the declaration is absent, which is the cleanest possible negative.
declarations.note: Systembolaget's name omits the range: the wine is Gérard Bertrand's 'Art de Vivre' Clairette du Languedoc Adissan, sold in a terracotta-look bottle. Searching 'Clairette du Languedoc Adissan' finds it; searching Systembolaget's string alone does not.

declarations.evidence: THE ESTATE'S ENTIRE RANGE WAS READ IN ONE FILE AND CONTAINS NO DECLARATION AND NO VINTAGE. Clos Cibonne, Chemin de la Cibonne, 83220 Le Pradet (Var), Côtes de Provence Cru Classé, is the producer for all six Swedish wines; Systembolaget's supplier is Robert Rask Vinhandel and the producer field is the estate itself. The site is a hand-built static site behind an age gate, on jQuery 1.6.4, with no robots.txt at all. Its per-wine pages (/fr/detail-bouteille.php?vin=1..8) are shells: every wine's content is loaded from a single file, /js/bouteilles-fr.js, which holds the complete range as a JS object. That file was fetched and read in full — eight cuvées, each with nom, type, category, region, title, desc, assemblage, degustation, complement and a PDF filename. THERE IS NO INGREDIENT FIELD, NO NUTRITION FIELD, NO ALLERGEN FIELD AND NO VINTAGE FIELD. The only vintage data on the whole site is a stale 'dispo: 2008 - 2010 - 2011 - 2012' on four cuvées. THE ONE PDF THAT COULD HAVE CARRIED IT CANNOT BE READ AND WOULD NOT HELP. declarations.name: Pur Carignan
declarations.evidence: THE ESTATE PUBLISHES A PER-CUVEE TECHNICAL SHEET AND IT IS NOT A DECLARATION. Château Revelette, Sandra & Peter Fischer, Chemin de Revelette, 13490 Jouques (Coteaux d'Aix-en-Provence); Systembolaget's supplier for all six wines is Prune AB and the producer field is the estate. The whole site is eight pages and /les-vins/ carries the entire range with vintages: Château Revelette Rouge 2022, Blanc 2023, Rosé 2023; Le Grand Blanc 2022, 2021, 2020; Le Grand Rouge 2020, 2019, 2017, 2015; Pur Carignan 2022, Pur Grenache 2022, Pur Blanc 2022; Coude à Coude Blanc, Rosé and Rouge 2023. Each links a 'fiche technique' PDF. ONE PDF WAS FETCHED AND SETTLES THE FORMAT FOR ALL OF THEM. ft-coude-a-coude-rose.pdf extracts cleanly and gives appellation, grape varieties, vinification, food pairing, bottling date (Avril 2024), alcohol (13,09), pH (3,36), total acidity (3,00 g/L), TOTAL SO2 (55 mg/L), residual sugar (<2) and 'Vin biologique, contrôle Ecocert, F-BIO-01'. It states a total SO2 figure, which is the closest thing to an additive statement on the site, and it still contains NO INGREDIENT LIST AND NO ENERGY VALUE. Under this project's rule a producer page counts only where it presents an actual list of substances; an analysis sheet is the same near-miss recorded for Von Winning and Weinland Rheingau in the German batch. No further PDFs were fetched — the format is the same for every cuvée and walking seventeen of them on a small estate's WordPress would be crawling. THE SITE ALSO RUNS BEHIND THE SHELF ON EVERY SINGLE CUVEE. Not one of the six Swedish vintages appears on it: the estate's newest published vintage for each of our wines is one or two years older. So even a real declaration here would have failed the vintage rule for all six. For this wine the estate's newest published Pur Carignan is the 2022.

declarations.evidence: THE ESTATE PUBLISHES A PER-VINTAGE FICHE FOR OUR EXACT WINES AND IT IS NOT A DECLARATION. Château d'Astros, Vidauban (Var), AOP Côtes-de-Provence; Systembolaget's supplier is Premier Taste Sweden AB and the producer field is the estate. Its WordPress site publishes one page per range and, from the Amour range page, a 'Fiche produit' link per wine per vintage — a WordPress slug that 302s to a dated PDF under /wp-content/uploads/. TWO OF THOSE PDFS WERE FETCHED AND BOTH ARE OUR EXACT VINTAGE: FT_PRINT_Amour_B_2024-FR.pdf ('BLANC 2024', 100 % Rolle) and F-T-Amour-2024-rouge-FR-.pdf ('ROUGE 2024', Grenache & Syrah). Both extract cleanly and both carry the same fields: a range story, tasting notes, vinification, serving temperature and food pairing. VINIFICATION SAYS ONLY 'Sulfitage maîtrisé et respectueux' — sulphiting described in prose, which is exactly the tasting-note mention this project's rules say not to accept. THERE IS NO INGREDIENT LIST, NO NUTRITION TABLE AND NO ENERGY VALUE ON EITHER. THE SEPARATE SHOPIFY SHOP DOES NOT CARRY ONE EITHER. boutique-chateauastros.com is a Shopify storefront on its own host (products allowed by robots.txt); its Amour Blanc product page was fetched — 470 kB of server-rendered HTML — and contains no ingredient, nutrition, allergen or e-label content of any kind. The shop has also rolled forward to the 2025 ('Amour blanc BIO 2025', 75 cl and 6×75 cl), so the shop is a vintage ahead of the fiches and of two of our three bottles. The FR (EU) pages were used throughout. For this wine the fiche is FT_PRINT_Amour_B_2024-FR.pdf, headed 'BLANC 2024', 100 % Rolle, matching Systembolaget 7007801 (Amour Blanc, 2024, 750 ml, 12,5 % vol, organic) on producer, cuvée and vintage. The vintage rule is satisfied and there is no ingredient list to attach.

_runs.batch: 1 — Marchesi Antinori, Chateau d'Esclans, Weingut Wittmann, The Sadie Family Wines (35 wines, vintage 2024+, not_declared)
1a — the 5 Marchesi Antinori wines whose e-label URL was already held, re-attempted under the robots.txt exception decided 2026-07-30
_runs.result: 5 pages fetched, 0 declarations read; the Scantrust e-label renders client-side and its data sits behind a per-request issued token. No status changed. The 4 wines with no e-label URL were not touched.

_runs.batch: 2 — rendering reconnaissance across five producers in four countries (Billaud-Simon FR, Tommasi IT, Hain DE, Hällåkra SE, Vini Franchetti IT), 27 wines, all vintage 2024+ and not_declared
_runs.result: 27 attempted, 3 found, 23 not found, 1 rejected. VERDICT: server-rendered e-labels do exist. Weingut Hain's are plain HTML on the Winitas shop platform at {winery}.winitas-shop.de/elabel/{id}, with the ingredient list, nutrition table, allergens and Impressum in the server's response — no JavaScript, no token, no robots restriction. Client-side rendering is therefore not universal, contrary to the worry raised by Scantrust and IMERO. The dominant finding is nevertheless scarcity: four of the five producers publish no e-label and no ingredient list anywhere this run could see, so the binding constraint is that e-labels are rare and unlinked, not that they are unreadable.

_runs.batch: 3 — German producers with 2024+ undeclared wines, worked one producer at a time and committed after each: Philipp Kuhn, Klosterhof, Doennhoff, Robert Weil, August Kesseler, Juelg, Kerpen, Von Winning, Schloss Johannisberg
_runs.result: in progress — Philipp Kuhn 3/3; Klosterhof 0/5 (rejected on vintage); Doennhoff 0/4; Robert Weil 0/3; August Kesseler 2/2 (graphic-druck); Hain 3/3 (Winitas); Wittmann 0/8; Juelg 2/2 (Winestro/nephele-s5); Kerpen 0/2; Von Winning 0/2 (client-side devworlds modal); Schloss Johannisberg 0/2 rejected on vintage (qrlabelinfo readable); Thanisch Erben Thanisch 2/2 (Winestro/winestro.info); Vier Jahreszeiten 1/2 (f-label by Euvino, robots exception used).

_runs.batch: 3c — five more German producers with 2024+ undeclared wines, committed one producer at a time: Weingut Philipps-Eckstein, Weingut Landerer, WG Gysler, Joh. Jos. Pruem, Ewald Theod. Drathen
_runs.result: 9 attempted, 1 found, 4 not found, 4 rejected. Philipps-Eckstein 0/2 (Winitas e-label readable but for the 2025; the Grauschiefer cuvee is in no vintage on the shop); Landerer 0/2 (IMERO e-label per wine, but the site keeps only the current 2025 release, and the litre bottling has no product page at all); Gysler 1/2 (NEW PLATFORM weinlabels.de, server-rendered, embedded as an IFRAME on the estate's own product page; the magnum of the same wine rejected because the e-label names a 0,75 l fill); Joh. Jos. Pruem 0/2 (the estate's entire website is a one-page contact card); Drathen 0/1 (no producer site; drathen.de fails TLS and redirects to a sister company). The rejections are all one of two shapes: the vintage on the shelf is a year behind the only release the producer still publishes, or the pack differs. Six of the nine wines belong to producers who demonstrably do publish e-labels; the declaration for the bottle actually on the Swedish shelf is what is missing.

_runs.batch: 3d — Weingut Steitz (recovering a find lost to a session limit in the previous run), then the whole of what remained of the German 2025 slice: Weingut Sebastian Erbeldinger, Weinland Rheingau eG, Andreas Oster Weinkellerei / HORIZN29, Bergkloster Winery, Ruppertsberger Weinkeller Hoheburg eG
_runs.result: 6 attempted, 2 found, 3 not found, 1 rejected, one producer each and a commit after each. Steitz 1/1 (Winestro at winestro.info/?s={token}, linked as 'Lebensmittelkennzeichnung' from a Wix product page that server-renders in full; the e-label states producer, wine, vintage, pack and alcohol itself and all five agreed). Andreas Oster 1/1 (elabel.apys.de, the platform first seen at Leitz, here yielding its first find; robots exception used because that host serves Disallow: / — five sibling products were checked to prove p2 is per-article, which is exactly the test Leitz failed). Sebastian Erbeldinger 0/1 REJECTED: a complete declaration published inline on the estate's own WooCommerce page, right cuvee, right vintage 2025, right pack, but 13,0 % vol against Systembolaget's 12,0 — outside the 0,5 % vol EU tolerance — and organic where Systembolaget is not. Weinland Rheingau 0/1, Ruppertsberger 0/1, Bergkloster 0/1: none of the three publishes an ingredient list anywhere, and in all three the specific Swedish bottling has no page on the producer's site at all. NOT ONE WINE WAS REJECTED ON VINTAGE, the first batch of which that is true, which confirms the 2025-first heuristic from the previous run. The German 2025 pool is now empty; 29 wines across 28 producers remain in the German 2024 pool.

_runs.batch: 3e — nine more German producers from the 2024-vintage pool, one commit each: Weingut Max Ferd. Richter (2 wines), Weingut Knipser, Weingut Balthasar Ress, Weingut Carl Loewen, Wagner-Stempel, Weingut Paulinshof, Weingut Andres, Weingut Hauck, In den Zehn Morgen, Dr. Bürklin-Wolf
_runs.result: 11 attempted, 0 found, 6 not found, 5 rejected. THE FIRST BATCH WITH NO FIND AT ALL, and the reason is uniform: seven of the ten producers demonstrably publish a complete declaration, and in every case it is for a vintage other than the one on the Swedish shelf. Rejections: Richter Sonnenlay (only the 2025 declared), Richter Wehlener Sonnenuhr (right vintage, wrong cuvée — the feinherb at 9,5 % against our fruity Kabinett at 7,5), Wagner-Stempel (graphic-druck e-label naming itself the 2025), Paulinshof (Euvino shop rolled to the 2025 at 12 % against our 11,5), Hauck (Winestro e-label naming itself the 2025 at 13,0 against our 12,5 Spätlese). Not founds: Knipser (declares everything, but no wine called 'Dry Riesling' and no 2024 dry Riesling at 12,5 %), Balthasar Ress (e-label exists and is Scantrust, unreadable by construction), Carl Loewen (per-vintage e-labels published as a DROPBOX FOLDER, including the 2024 — not fetched, Dropbox disallows /scl/ and is not a host the e-label exception reaches), Andres (declares inline on its Magento shop, but the Haardt Chardonnay is a trade bottling absent from shop and price list), In den Zehn Morgen (EuvinoPRO shop with the ingredient fields left empty on every product), Bürklin-Wolf (whole Premier Cru range listed at the 2022, and no ingredient list on any page). NEW PLATFORM: EuvinoPRO, three shops in this batch, with the declaration inline on the product page. Scantrust seen on a German producer for the first time. Nine producers, zero attachable declarations — the constraint in the German 2024 slice is now purely the vintage.

_runs.batch: 3c — Carl Loewen re-attempted under the widened robots.txt exception (a producer's own file on a general host), then the rest of the German 2024 pool
_runs.result: in progress — Carl Loewen 9601001 not_found -> found. Gröhl 0/1. Bioweingut Lorenz 0/1. Corvers-Kauter 0/1. August Eser / Knyphausen 0/1 (vintage). Benzinger 0/1 (vintage, and IMERO).

_runs.batch: 3f — the last of the German 2024-vintage undeclared pool, one commit per producer: Weingüter Wegeler, Weingut Hoffmann-Simon, Weingut Keller, Emrich-Schönleber, Spring Wine & Spirits / Weingut Mehrlein, Solera Sweden (2 wines), Rewine, Joh. Jos. Prüm. THE GERMAN 2024+ POOL IS NOW EXHAUSTED.
_runs.result: 9 attempted, 0 found, 8 not found, 1 rejected. THE REJECTION: Hoffmann-Simon, a complete self-identifying Winitas e-label for exactly this cuvée — Klüsserather Bruderschaft Riesling Spätlese trocken, Bio-Weintrauben, 322 kJ/77 kcal — naming itself the 2025 where the shelf holds the 2024; the Winitas one-request vintage census proved the 2024 is on no listing the estate publishes. THE NOT FOUNDS SPLIT THREE WAYS. (1) Producer found, current vintage on sale, no declaration published: Wegeler, whose Shopware shop has per-wine pages, per-vintage URLs and our exact 2024 at 12,0 % vol to the decimal, and links nothing but 'enthält Sulphite' — the clearest evidence yet that structure does not predict publication. (2) Estate with no searchable surface: Keller (a three-URL Wix brochure, from Gault Millau's Winzer des Jahrzehnts) and Prüm (a 3,7 kB contact card, third wine, re-fetched rather than assumed). (3) Importer in the producer field: four wines. Spring's Even & Odd was traced to Weingut Mehrlein via the agency's own 'Producent' field, and Mehrlein's site states outright that it vinifies exclusively for trade partners, so the cuvée has no page to begin with; Rewine's Robusta is absent from both of that importer's sitemaps; Solera's Pride and Phonetics are own labels whose estate could not be established at all, and nothing was guessed from the two German bottlers on Solera's producer list. ONE OUTAGE, RECORDED AS SUCH: emrich-schoenleber.de answered 503 on every content URL across three requests — an outage, not a refusal — and a German retailer carries what is very probably the producer's own text for our exact vintage and alcohol. It was not taken. A retailer's transcription cannot be allowed to outrank Systembolaget's in a file that outranks Systembolaget's. That wine is the strongest revisit candidate in the pool. WHAT THE WHOLE GERMAN POOL CAME TO: 89 wines across some 60 producers attempted, 18 declarations attached.

_runs.batch: 3g — FRANCE OPENS. Château du Galoupet (Moët Hennessy), 2 wines, both vintage 2025
_runs.result: 2 attempted, 0 found, 2 not found, 0 rejected. The estate publishes one page per wine per vintage and both 2025 pages are live and match Systembolaget on vintage, alcohol and organic status — the vintage rule is satisfied and the ingredient list is simply not there. Its 'Plateforme de Transparence' links respect-code.org traceability pages for the 2021-2023 Cru Classé only, which is neither a declaration nor our vintage. HOST NOTE: galoupet.com resolves but refuses port 443; the live host is www.chateaugaloupet.com, reached via the plain-http 301.

_runs.batch: 3g — M. Chapoutier, 4 wines (Marius Vermentino Terret 2025, Marius Rosé 2025, Marius Grenache Syrah 2025, Les Vignes de Bila-Haut 2024)
_runs.result: 4 attempted, 0 found, 4 not found, 0 rejected. THE HOST REFUSES. www.chapoutier.com serves a permissive robots.txt and then answers HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare managed challenge on every content URL, including the sitemap its own robots.txt names. A challenge is a technological measure and absolute; two requests, no workaround, stop. No alternative host: Bila-Haut and Marius are both published under chapoutier.com and no separate domain resolves. FIRST CLOUDFLARE CHALLENGE IN THIS PROJECT — French estates are more likely to sit behind one than German ones were.

_runs.batch: 3g — Gérard Bertrand, 3 wines (Clairette du Languedoc Adissan 2024, Côte des Roses rosé 2025, Gris Blanc rosé 2024 magnum)
_runs.result: 3 attempted, 0 found, 3 not found, 0 rejected. THE CLEANEST NEGATIVE IN THE FILE SO FAR. A 581-product Shopify catalogue keyed by cuvee, vintage and format; the exact page for two of the three wines exists at our exact vintage and pack; and a grep of both pages for nine declaration keywords returns nothing at all. 212 site pages, none about ingredients; 73 Shopify metaobjects, all estates, distributors and recipes. The per-product CDN datasheet PDF is the Von Winning near-miss again — vinification and tasting notes, no list. Scale and structure predict publication no better in France than in Germany.

_runs.batch: 3g — Clos Cibonne, 6 wines (Cuvée Tradition 2024 in 750 and 1500, Tentations 2025, Cuvée Caroline 2024, Cuvée Spéciale Tibouren 2025 in 750 and 1500)
_runs.result: 6 attempted, 0 found, 6 not found, 0 rejected. A hand-built static site on jQuery 1.6.4 behind an age gate, no robots.txt, whose per-wine pages are shells: the whole range lives in one 7,9 kB /js/bouteilles-fr.js object with fields for grapes, tasting notes and a PDF name and NO ingredient, nutrition, allergen or vintage field. The only vintages named on the entire site are 'dispo: 2008 - 2010 - 2011 - 2012'. The per-cuvée Fiche Technique PDF is a 2 MB image scan with no extractable text and no date. Also a cuvée-name mismatch: Systembolaget's 'Cuvée Spéciale Tibouren' has no counterpart in the estate's own eight-wine range.

_runs.batch: 3g — Château Revelette, 6 wines (Pur Carignan 2024, Pur Blanc 2024, Le Grand Blanc 2024, Coude à Coude Rosé 2024, Rouge 2024 and Blanc 2025)
_runs.result: 6 attempted, 0 found, 6 not found, 0 rejected. An eight-page WordPress site with the whole range and a fiche technique PDF per cuvée. One PDF was fetched and settles the format: appellation, grapes, vinification, bottling date, alcohol, pH, total acidity, TOTAL SO2 and residual sugar — and no ingredient list and no energy value. THE FRENCH NEAR-MISS SHAPE IS THE 'FICHE TECHNIQUE', and unlike the German ones it even names an SO2 figure, which makes it look more like a declaration than it is. The site is also one or two vintages behind Systembolaget on every one of the six cuvées.

_runs.batch: 3g — Saget la Perrière, 4 wines (Sancerre La Perrière 2024, La Petite Perrière Sauvignon Blanc 2025, Pinot Noir Rosé 2025, Pinot Noir 2024)
_runs.result: 4 attempted, 0 found, 4 not found, 0 rejected. A Loire house of real size whose site has NO product pages: twenty editorial URLs and nothing else, on both .com and .fr. Three of the four wines are the export brand La Petite Perrière, which does not appear on the producer's site at all. The house's 'Presse' media site was checked for the Carl Loewen Download-Center pattern and has brochures and logos, no eLabels. NOTABLE NEGATIVE FINDING: a German retailer (vinello.eu) publishes a full ingredient list for La Petite Perrière Sauvignon. It was not used and must not be — a retailer in another country is explicitly not a source under this project's rules — and it is recorded so a later run does not mistake it for a find.

_runs.batch: 3g — Château d'Astros, 3 wines (Amour Blanc 2024, Amour Rouge 2024, Amour Rosé 2025)
_runs.result: 3 attempted, 0 found, 3 not found, 0 rejected. The estate documents its wines per vintage — 'Fiche produit' slugs that 302 to dated PDFs — and TWO OF THE THREE SWEDISH WINES HAVE THEIR OWN 2024 FICHE, our exact vintage. Both were read in full and neither has an ingredient list, a nutrition table or an energy value; their only additive-adjacent words are the prose 'Sulfitage maîtrisé et respectueux'. Its separate Shopify shop (boutique-chateauastros.com) carries nothing either and has already rolled to the 2025. CLOSES THE FRENCH BATCH ON THE SAME SHAPE AS REVELETTE: in France the near-miss is the fiche technique, and the vintage often matches, which makes the absence of a declaration the finding rather than a side effect of stale stock.

_runs.batch: 3h — Domaine Denis Père & Fils, 6 wines (Corton-Charlemagne Grand Cru, Pernand-Vergelesses 1er Cru Sous Frétille, Pernand-Vergelesses Blanc, Pernand-Vergelesses Rouge, Bourgogne Aligoté, Bourgogne Pinot Noir, all 2024)
_runs.result: 6 attempted, 0 found, 6 not found, 0 rejected. A 14 ha Côte de Beaune estate whose entire web presence is a three-page Avada/WordPress marketing site with no webshop and no per-wine page. Its whole range lives on ONE page, /decouvrez-nos-appellations/, which names every one of our six appellations and carries no ingredient list, no nutrition table and no e-label link. Cheapest possible negative: three requests settled six wines. The Burgundy shape to expect — the estate sells through the négoce and importers, so there is nothing consumer-facing to hang a QR destination on.
